min_price.label: Min Price
min_price.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
min_price.whenToUse: "Do I want to exclude penny stocks and micro-cap junk?" Extremely low-priced stocks are prone to manipulation, extreme volatility, and poor liquidity. The SEC classifies sub-$5 stocks as penny stocks for a reason.
min_price.howToRead: min_price=5000 passes stocks at 5,000 KRW or above. For US markets, $5 is the standard penny stock threshold. Most institutional investors exclude stocks below $10.
min_price.caution: Legitimate companies can temporarily trade at low prices due to bad news. Combine with market cap filters for more meaningful size screening. Price alone is not a quality indicator.

max_price.label: Max Price
max_price.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
max_price.whenToUse: "Do I want to exclude stocks above a certain absolute price?" A practical filter for investors with lot-size constraints or those targeting a specific price tier for portfolio construction.
max_price.howToRead: max_price=100000 passes stocks priced at 100,000 KRW or below. For US markets, set appropriately (e.g., 500 USD). Absolute price is mainly a liquidity/accessibility criterion, not a valuation metric.
max_price.caution: Absolute stock price is unrelated to company value — it depends entirely on share count and stock splits. Market cap or PE are far more meaningful for valuation. Use price filters only for practical access reasons.

price_range.label: Price Range
price_range.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
price_range.whenToUse: "I want stocks within a specific price band." Combines min_price and max_price into a single filter — useful for targeting specific tiers (mid-caps by price, options-friendly names, etc.).
price_range.howToRead: min=10000, max=50000 passes stocks priced 10,000-50,000 KRW. For US: min=10, max=200 is a common institutional range. Essentially a convenience wrapper around the separate min/max price filters.
price_range.caution: Price bands don't map to company size or quality — stock splits change price without changing value. Market cap filters are almost always more meaningful for actual portfolio construction.

price_change.label: Price Change %
price_change.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
price_change.whenToUse: "How much has the stock moved over N days?" The most general-purpose price filter — set min/max to capture any range of gains or losses. Use for finding surging stocks, avoiding crashers, or any directional screen.
price_change.howToRead: days=1 checks one-day change. min=3, max=10 captures stocks up 3-10%. min=-5 finds stocks down 5%+. Combine days and thresholds freely to target any price-action pattern.
price_change.caution: Raw price change reveals nothing about the cause — earnings, news, sector rotation, and market beta all blend together. Always combine with volume or fundamental filters to separate signal from noise.

return_turnaround.label: Return Turnaround
return_turnaround.desc: Prev N-day return <= threshold and recent N-day return >= threshold
return_turnaround.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
return_turnaround.whenToUse: "A V-shaped reversal pattern — has the stock bounced sharply after a decline?" Automated detection of the decline-then-rally pattern favored by mean-reversion traders seeking oversold bounces.
return_turnaround.howToRead: prev_max_return_pct=-2 and min_return_pct=2 passes stocks that fell 2%+ over 5 days and then rallied 2%+ over the next 5 days. Raising thresholds to 5% captures only dramatic turnarounds.
return_turnaround.caution: A simple V-bounce can be a dead-cat bounce — a brief rebound before continuation of the decline. Check whether the catalyst for the decline has been resolved. Rising volume on the bounce side adds credibility.

min_volume.label: Min Volume
min_volume.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
min_volume.whenToUse: "Can I actually execute trades in this stock without excessive slippage?" Minimum daily volume is the most basic liquidity gate. Without sufficient volume, backtest results are fiction and real-world execution is painful.
min_volume.howToRead: min_volume=100000 passes stocks trading 100,000+ shares daily. Adjust by market: Korean small-caps at 50K, US large-caps at 500K. Dollar volume (avg_trading_value) is a more precise liquidity measure.
min_volume.caution: Volume alone can't distinguish low-price high-volume from high-price low-volume stocks — dollar volume is better. Also beware theme-driven temporary volume spikes that revert once hype fades.

volume_above_avg.label: Volume Above Avg
volume_above_avg.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
volume_above_avg.whenToUse: "Is today's volume elevated above its recent average?" Above-average volume confirms that price moves are backed by participation. The fundamental principle: volume validates direction.
volume_above_avg.howToRead: multiplier=1.0 passes stocks at or above their 20-day average volume. At 1.5 (150%), conviction is higher; 2.0 is a clear surge. Price up + volume up = bullish confirmation. Price down + volume up = bearish capitulation.
volume_above_avg.caution: Volume can surge on selling just as easily as buying — always pair with price direction. Index rebalancing, options expiration, and block trades create mechanical volume spikes that carry no directional information.

volume_spike.label: Volume Spike
volume_spike.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
volume_spike.whenToUse: "Has volume suddenly exploded — something is happening?" A volume spike is the market screaming that attention has arrived. The starting gun for breakouts, reversals, or news-driven moves.
volume_spike.howToRead: multiplier=1.5 passes stocks at 150%+ of 20-day average volume. At 2.0 it is a significant spike; 3.0 is dramatic. Combine with price direction: up + spike = bullish conviction; down + spike = panic selling.
volume_spike.caution: A volume spike alone is directionless — it could be buying or selling. Check the cause: earnings, M&A rumor, theme momentum, or a large block trade. Single block trades may not reflect organic interest.

ma_touch.label: MA Touch
ma_touch.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
ma_touch.whenToUse: "Is price pulling back to touch a long-term MA — a dip-buy opportunity in an uptrend?" A 120-day MA touch during an established uptrend represents a healthy correction and potential re-entry point, not a trend reversal.
ma_touch.howToRead: threshold=0.02 passes stocks within 2% of the 120-day MA. At 1%, only stocks nearly touching the MA qualify. At 5%, the band is wider. The MA acts as a dynamic support level.
ma_touch.caution: If the MA is broken to the downside, "support" fails — what looked like a buy-the-dip turns into a breakdown. Confirm with RSI approaching oversold or declining volume (seller fatigue) before entering. Always combine with above_ma.

above_ma.label: Above MA
above_ma.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
above_ma.whenToUse: "Is this stock in an uptrend?" Being above the moving average means buying pressure exceeds selling. The most fundamental first filter for trend-following strategies.
above_ma.howToRead: period=20 passes stocks above the 20-day MA. Raise min_distance_pct to 2 for stocks "firmly" above it. Use period=50 or 200 for medium/long-term trend confirmation.
above_ma.caution: Stocks barely above the MA can slip below the next day. In sideways markets, prices whipsaw above/below the MA constantly. Pair with ADX or volume filters for reliability.

below_ma.label: Below MA
below_ma.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
below_ma.whenToUse: "Looking for stocks in a downtrend or oversold bounce candidates." Filters stocks below their MA — for short strategies or contrarian "fallen angel" plays.
below_ma.howToRead: period=20 passes stocks below the 20-day MA. max_distance_pct=-10 = stocks more than 10% below MA (deep selloff). period=200 for long-term downtrend.
below_ma.caution: Classic "catching a falling knife" trap. Below MA doesn't mean cheap — further decline is possible. Always pair with volume surge, RSI reversal or other bottom confirmation signals.

ma_cross_up.label: MA Cross Up
ma_cross_up.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
ma_cross_up.whenToUse: "Has the very short-term MA crossed above the short-term — signaling fresh buying momentum?" A 5/20 golden cross is a fast-reacting swing-trading entry signal for capturing the start of short-term rallies.
ma_cross_up.howToRead: lookback_days=5 passes stocks with a 5/20 golden cross in the last 5 days. This signal fires much more frequently than 50/200 crosses, making it suited to active traders.
ma_cross_up.caution: The 5/20 cross is so short-term that whipsaw reversals within a week are common. Never trade this signal alone — require accompanying volume expansion or ADX confirmation to filter noise.

ma_cross_down.label: MA Cross Down
ma_cross_down.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
ma_cross_down.whenToUse: "Has the medium-term MA crossed below the longer-term — a bearish trend shift?" A 20/60 dead cross signals deteriorating medium-term momentum. Useful as a sell trigger or risk-warning filter.
ma_cross_down.howToRead: lookback_days=5 passes stocks where the 20-day MA crossed below the 60-day MA in the last 5 days. Reacts faster than the 50/200 death cross, serving as an early warning for position exits.
ma_cross_down.caution: Short/medium-period crosses generate far more false signals than long-period crosses. Especially meaningless when ADX is below 20. Waiting 1-2 days after the cross to confirm improves accuracy.

rsi_oversold.label: RSI Oversold
rsi_oversold.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
rsi_oversold.whenToUse: "Has selling been extreme enough that a bounce is likely?" RSI below 30-35 signals potential seller exhaustion — a core entry condition for mean-reversion strategies. The most popular oscillator-based buy signal.
rsi_oversold.howToRead: threshold=35 passes stocks with RSI at or below 35 (moderately oversold). At 30, it is textbook oversold; at 20, it is extreme. Mean-reversion strategies rely heavily on this zone for entry.
rsi_oversold.caution: Oversold does not guarantee a bounce — the most common beginner mistake. In strong downtrends, RSI can stay below 20 for weeks. Always confirm the broader trend (MA, ADX) is not firmly bearish before buying oversold stocks.

rsi_overbought.label: RSI Overbought
rsi_overbought.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
rsi_overbought.whenToUse: "Is this stock overheated and due for a breather?" RSI above 70 is the textbook overbought zone — selling pressure tends to build as short-term traders take profits. Flag for caution, not necessarily immediate sale.
rsi_overbought.howToRead: threshold=70 passes stocks with RSI 70+. At 80, the condition is extreme. Use for profit-taking timing on existing positions, or for identifying short candidates when confirmed by other bearish signals.
rsi_overbought.caution: In strong uptrends, RSI can sustain above 80 for weeks — overbought does not mean over. Selling solely because RSI is 70+ will cause you to exit big winners prematurely. Judge alongside trend strength.

rsi_range.label: RSI Range
rsi_range.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
rsi_range.whenToUse: "Is RSI in the healthy trending zone — not overbought, not oversold?" RSI 50-70 characterizes a stock in an active uptrend's cruising altitude — momentum is alive but not overextended. Ideal for trend-following filters.
rsi_range.howToRead: lower=50, upper=70 passes stocks with RSI between 50 and 70 — the sweet spot for healthy uptrends. 40-60 filters for neutral-zone stocks. Narrower ranges reduce the pass rate significantly.
rsi_range.caution: Too-narrow RSI windows yield very few matches. RSI converges to 50 in sideways markets even without price change, so a stock at RSI 55 could be trending or flat. Always verify with price trend indicators.

bollinger_width.label: Bollinger Width
bollinger_width.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
bollinger_width.whenToUse: "Is volatility extremely low, signaling an imminent big move?" Narrow bands = market undecided, accumulating energy. Used to detect accumulation phases before breakouts.
bollinger_width.howToRead: max_width_pct=15 passes stocks with band width under 15% of price. Under 10% is notably narrow; under 5% is historic squeeze level. Breakout direction needs a separate filter.
bollinger_width.caution: Band width alone can't predict direction. Squeeze states can persist for weeks or months — timing is uncertain. Rising OBV during squeeze suggests accumulation; falling OBV suggests distribution.

volume_below_avg.label: Volume Below Avg
volume_below_avg.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
volume_below_avg.whenToUse: "Is volume drying up — signaling either stealth accumulation or total disinterest?" Below-average volume paired with narrowing price range may indicate quiet accumulation; with declining price, it suggests selling fatigue.
volume_below_avg.howToRead: multiplier=1.0 passes stocks below their 20-day average volume. At 0.5, volume is less than half the norm — extreme quietness. Combine with Bollinger width for squeeze detection and OBV direction for accumulation hints.
volume_below_avg.caution: The critical distinction is accumulation vs indifference. If OBV and CMF are simultaneously rising, quiet accumulation is likely. If both are flat or declining, the stock is simply being ignored.

price_flat.label: Price Flat
price_flat.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
price_flat.whenToUse: "Is the stock trading in a tight range — a coiled spring before a big move?" Flat price within a narrow band signals energy accumulation. Can indicate stealth accumulation (if OBV rises) or distribution (if OBV falls).
price_flat.howToRead: max_range_pct=10 passes stocks with less than 10% high-low range over 20 days. At 5%, the stock is in extreme consolidation. Combine with OBV direction to infer whether accumulation or distribution is occurring.
price_flat.caution: Consolidation can last weeks to months with no resolution — tying up capital with no return. Always pair with a breakout signal to time exits from the range. Without a catalyst, flat stocks may stay flat.

obv_trend.label: OBV Trend
obv_trend.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
obv_trend.whenToUse: "Is volume flow consistently favoring buyers?" An upward OBV trend means up-days consistently attract more volume than down-days — the most intuitive measure of money flowing in.
obv_trend.howToRead: direction=up passes stocks where OBV has been rising over 20 days. lookback=10 for short-term, 40 for medium-term flow. Price and OBV rising together confirms a healthy trend.
obv_trend.caution: OBV treats any positive close day equally — a 0.01% gain adds the full day's volume to the up side. This can overstate accumulation in choppy markets. Cross-verify with CMF which weights by closing position within the range.

stochastic_level.label: Stochastic Level
stochastic_level.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
stochastic_level.whenToUse: "Is Stochastic in the oversold zone — is price near the bottom of its recent range?" %K below 20 means the current close is near the lowest point in the lookback period. Used for accumulation-zone detection and contrarian entries.
stochastic_level.howToRead: threshold=20, condition=below passes stocks with %K under 20. At 10, the condition is extreme. Switch to condition=above with threshold=80 for overbought detection. Effective as an accumulation-phase filter.
stochastic_level.caution: Stochastic can become stuck below 20 in strong downtrends, printing oversold for weeks without a bounce. Oversold does not equal reversal. Watch for declining volume (selling exhaustion) and price stabilization before entering.

vpci_trend.label: VPCI Trend
vpci_trend.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
vpci_trend.whenToUse: "Is volume genuinely confirming the price trend?" A rising VPCI means volume is flowing in the direction of price — the trend is backed up by real participation, not just thin-air drift.
vpci_trend.howToRead: direction=up passes stocks with rising VPCI over 10 days. VPCI up + price up = confirmed healthy rally. Price up + VPCI down = hollow rally, warning of potential reversal.
vpci_trend.caution: VPCI, OBV, and CMF all measure similar things — using all three creates redundant filtering. Pick 1-2 based on backtest performance. Overlapping volume indicators can over-filter your universe without adding new information.

obv_divergence.label: OBV Divergence
obv_divergence.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
obv_divergence.whenToUse: "Is price flat while volume is quietly accumulating in one direction?" OBV divergence — price sideways but OBV rising — is a classic signal of stealth accumulation before a major move.
obv_divergence.howToRead: price_max_range_pct=5 with obv_min_change_pct=5 passes stocks whose price stayed within 5% over 20 days while OBV moved 5%+. Rising OBV = accumulation; falling OBV = quiet distribution.
obv_divergence.caution: Divergence timing is notoriously uncertain — accumulation can last weeks or months before price reacts. Combine with a breakout trigger (breakout_with_volume) to get actionable entry signals rather than just early warnings.

stochastic_divergence.label: Stochastic Divergence
stochastic_divergence.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
stochastic_divergence.whenToUse: "Price is making new lows but Stochastic is making higher lows — hidden buying?" Bullish divergence signals that downward momentum is fading even as price declines. A reversal early-warning pattern near market bottoms.
stochastic_divergence.howToRead: lookback=20 scans for divergence over 20 days. divergence_threshold=5 requires %K to be at least 5 points higher than the prior swing low while price is lower. Higher thresholds mean fewer but more reliable signals.
stochastic_divergence.caution: Divergence timing is notoriously imprecise — price can keep falling for weeks after the divergence appears. Treat as a warning flag, not an entry trigger. Wait for actual price reversal (bullish candle, support hold) before entering.

vpci_divergence.label: VPCI Divergence
vpci_divergence.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
vpci_divergence.whenToUse: "Price is flat but the volume-price relationship is shifting — invisible accumulation?" VPCI divergence is a more refined version of OBV divergence, measuring whether volume confirms or denies price moves with greater precision.
vpci_divergence.howToRead: price_max_range_pct=5 passes stocks flat within 5% over 20 days where VPCI direction has changed. Compared to OBV divergence, VPCI gives more weight to the location of the close within the day's range.
vpci_divergence.caution: VPCI is a less commonly used indicator, so fewer traders watch it and the self-fulfilling effect is weaker. Cross-verify with OBV or CMF. As with all divergence signals, timing remains the key uncertainty.

bottom_breakout.label: Bottom Breakout
bottom_breakout.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
bottom_breakout.whenToUse: "Catch stocks breaking below their low — for shorting or risk management." Filters stocks that breach their period low. Used for short strategies or "avoid this stock" screening.
bottom_breakout.howToRead: lookback_days=20, breakout_pct=5 passes stocks that fell 5%+ below their 20-day low. Can also find extreme oversold candidates for contrarian plays (high risk).
bottom_breakout.caution: Hard to tell if a bottom break is a trend change or temporary panic. High volume = panic selling possibility. Check if post-earnings gap-down. Always set stop-losses for contrarian entries.

fresh_breakout.label: Fresh Breakout
fresh_breakout.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
fresh_breakout.whenToUse: "Is this the first breakout, or has the stock been above the breakout level for days already?" Captures only the initial breakout to avoid chasing a move that's already extended.
fresh_breakout.howToRead: breakout_pct=5 passes stocks breaking 5%+ above their 20-day high for the first time. Stocks already 3 days into a breakout are excluded. Extracts the freshest momentum signals only.
fresh_breakout.caution: Even a first-day breakout can fail the next day (fake breakout). Volume confirmation is essential. Closing-price breakouts are more reliable than intraday wicks that revert by close.

breakout_with_volume.label: Breakout + Volume
breakout_with_volume.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
breakout_with_volume.whenToUse: "Is this a real breakout backed by volume?" Price breakout + volume surge confirmed simultaneously. The foundational technical analysis principle: breakouts without volume are likely false.
breakout_with_volume.howToRead: breakout_pct=5 + volume_ratio=1.5 = 5% above 20-day high with 1.5x average volume. fresh_only=True catches only the first breakout (prevents chasing repeated signals).
breakout_with_volume.caution: Setting volume_ratio too high (3.0+) catches only earnings/news events, missing technical breakouts. fresh_only=True is essential — stocks already days into a breakout carry chase risk.

resistance_breakout.label: Resistance Breakout
resistance_breakout.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
resistance_breakout.whenToUse: "Has price broken above the recent high — a classic buy signal?" Breaking past a resistance level (prior high) means the selling wall has been absorbed. The most fundamental technical buy trigger.
resistance_breakout.howToRead: lookback_days=20 captures breakouts above the 20-day high. breakout_margin_pct=1 adds a 1% buffer to filter noise. At 60 days, you're testing medium-term resistance. Multi-tested resistance breaks carry more significance.
resistance_breakout.caution: Profit-taking just above resistance is extremely common — price may reverse right after breaking out. Volume confirmation is essential. Resistance that has been tested 2-3 times before breaking is more meaningful.

pe_ratio.label: P/E Ratio
pe_ratio.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
pe_ratio.whenToUse: "How many years of current earnings does the stock price represent?" The most universally used valuation metric. At PE 15, you're paying 15 years' worth of current earnings for the stock.
pe_ratio.howToRead: max_pe=15 passes stocks at 15x earnings or below. S&P 500 historical average: 15-17x; KOSPI average: 10-12x. Growth stocks trade at 30-50x while deep-value names sit below 10x.
pe_ratio.caution: Loss-making companies have negative PE (meaningless) — always filter for positive earnings first. One-time gains can artificially depress PE. Forward PE (based on estimated future earnings) is more useful but harder to obtain reliably.

pb_ratio.label: P/B Ratio
pb_ratio.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
pb_ratio.whenToUse: "How much am I paying relative to the company's net assets?" PBR below 1.0 means the market values the firm below its liquidation value — the classic Graham-Buffett deep-value signal.
pb_ratio.howToRead: max_pb=1.5 passes stocks at 1.5x book value or less. Below 1.0 is cheaper than breakup value. Banks: 0.5-1.0, tech: 3-10. exclude_negative_bv=True removes equity-negative firms (capital erosion).
pb_ratio.caution: Intangible-heavy businesses (software, brands, pharma IP) have book values that dramatically understate real worth — high PBR is normal, not overvalued. PBR is most meaningful for tangible-asset sectors (banks, REITs, construction).

ps_ratio.label: P/S Ratio
ps_ratio.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
ps_ratio.whenToUse: "Is this stock cheap relative to its revenue?" P/S works even for unprofitable companies since revenue is harder to manipulate than earnings. Popularized by Ken Fisher as a valuation safety net.
ps_ratio.howToRead: max_ps=2 passes stocks trading below 2x sales. Manufacturing: 0.5-1.5x, SaaS: 5-15x, biotech: 50x+ is not unusual. Sector context is absolutely mandatory when interpreting P/S.
ps_ratio.caution: Low P/S on a permanently unprofitable company is a trap — cheap but worthless. Combine with operating margin or FCF margin. High revenue growth can justify higher P/S multiples (growth premium).

pcf_ratio.label: P/CF Ratio
pcf_ratio.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
pcf_ratio.whenToUse: "Is this stock cheap relative to its operating cash flow?" P/CF uses cash flow instead of earnings, making it immune to depreciation policy differences across companies. More stable than PE for cross-company comparison.
pcf_ratio.howToRead: max_pcf=10 passes stocks at 10x operating cash flow or below. Under 7 is notably cheap. Because depreciation doesn't affect OCF, asset-heavy companies with differing depreciation schedules can be compared fairly.
pcf_ratio.caution: Operating cash flow swings with working capital changes (receivables, inventory), creating quarter-to-quarter noise. Use annual figures. Since OCF excludes capex, capital-intensive firms may look cheap here but expensive on FCF yield.

dividend_yield.label: Dividend Yield
dividend_yield.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
dividend_yield.whenToUse: "Do I want steady cash income from my holdings?" Dividend yield measures annual dividends relative to price — the foundation of income and retirement portfolios.
dividend_yield.howToRead: min_yield=3 passes stocks paying 3%+ annually. Set max_yield to 8-10 to exclude distressed names with unsustainable payouts. S&P 500 averages 1.5-2%.
dividend_yield.caution: A high yield caused by a collapsing stock price is a yield trap, not a bargain. Also watch for special one-time dividends inflating the figure. Use regular dividends only.

drawdown_from_high.label: Drawdown From High
drawdown_from_high.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
drawdown_from_high.whenToUse: "How far has this stock fallen from its recent peak?" A drawdown filter for contrarian buy-the-dip strategies or, inversely, for excluding stocks with large recent losses.
drawdown_from_high.howToRead: min_drop_pct=20 passes stocks that have fallen 20%+ from their 120-day high. For risk management (exclusion), use as a negative filter. At 10%, it catches early warning-level pullbacks.
drawdown_from_high.caution: A 20% drop may be a buying opportunity or the start of a deeper decline — impossible to know in advance. If caused by deteriorating earnings or structural industry shifts, it is a value trap. Always verify positive FCF and manageable debt first.

earnings_yield.label: Earnings Yield
earnings_yield.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
earnings_yield.whenToUse: "Is this stock a better deal than bonds?" Earnings Yield (=1/PE) converts equity valuation into a yield directly comparable to bond rates. A core variable in Greenblatt's Magic Formula.
earnings_yield.howToRead: min_yield=8 passes stocks earning 8%+ on their price (roughly PE 12.5x or lower). Compare against the risk-free rate — if treasuries pay 4%, an 8% EY implies a 4% equity risk premium.
earnings_yield.caution: One-time gains (asset sales, currency windfalls) inflate EPS and thus EY. Verify earnings are normalized and recurring. Negative earnings make the metric meaningless.

ebit_ev.label: EBIT/EV
ebit_ev.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
ebit_ev.whenToUse: "What is the operating yield on this enterprise?" Greenblatt's Magic Formula core metric. EBIT/EV strips out tax regimes and capital structure to reveal pure business profitability relative to total acquisition cost.
ebit_ev.howToRead: min_ebit_ev=10 passes stocks with EBIT/EV above 10%. At 15%+, the business is notably cheap. In the Magic Formula, stocks are ranked by this ratio combined with ROIC.
ebit_ev.caution: Cash-rich companies have lower EV, boosting the ratio — that's a genuine positive. But if EBIT includes non-recurring operating items, it overstates real yield. Verify operating income continuity.

fcf_yield.label: FCF Yield
fcf_yield.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
fcf_yield.whenToUse: "What real cash return does this stock generate relative to its market cap?" FCF Yield is the closest proxy to a stock's true earnings power — the cash available for dividends, buybacks, and debt reduction.
fcf_yield.howToRead: min_fcf_yield=5 passes stocks generating free cash flow equal to 5%+ of market cap. At 8%+ the name is highly attractive. Compare against bond yields: a higher FCF yield signals equities are cheap relative to fixed income.
fcf_yield.caution: A single year of heavy capex can temporarily crush FCF — use a 3-year average for stability. Working capital swings also distort quarterly figures. Always use annual data.

peg_ratio.label: PEG Ratio
peg_ratio.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
peg_ratio.whenToUse: "Is the PE justified by the growth rate?" PEG = PE / EPS growth rate. Popularized by Peter Lynch. Below 1.0 means you're paying less than one times growth — the gold standard for GARP investing.
peg_ratio.howToRead: max_peg=1.0 passes stocks with PEG at or below 1.0 — growth-adjusted fair value. At 0.5, the stock is significantly underpriced relative to growth. Complements PE by accounting for earnings trajectory.
peg_ratio.caution: Negative EPS growth makes PEG negative (meaningless). The result depends entirely on which growth rate is used (trailing vs forward consensus), and forward estimates carry analyst bias. Specify the growth-rate source clearly.

debt_to_equity.label: D/E Ratio
debt_to_equity.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
debt_to_equity.whenToUse: "How much borrowed money vs. own money?" High D/E = high leverage — magnifies both gains and losses, with higher bankruptcy risk.
debt_to_equity.howToRead: max_de=100 passes firms with debt ratio under 100% (debt = equity). Below 50 is conservative; above 200 is high leverage. IT 30-50% is already high; utilities 100-200% is normal.
debt_to_equity.caution: Financials/utilities/telecoms are structurally high-debt by business model — never apply blanket thresholds. Negative equity (capital erosion) makes D/E negative, potentially passing the filter erroneously.

current_ratio.label: Current Ratio
current_ratio.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
current_ratio.whenToUse: "Can this company pay its bills due within one year?" Current Ratio = Current Assets / Current Liabilities. Below 1.0 = potential short-term liquidity crisis. The most basic survival metric.
current_ratio.howToRead: min=1.0 passes firms with more current assets than liabilities. 1.5-2.0 is healthy. max=3.0 excludes inefficiently high ratios. Manufacturing ~1.5+; IT ~2.0+ is typical.
current_ratio.caution: Too high may indicate cash hoarding without reinvestment. High inventory inflates the ratio but isn't easily liquidated. Check quick ratio alongside for accuracy.

roe.label: ROE
roe.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
roe.whenToUse: "How much profit does this company earn on shareholders' equity?" Buffett's signature metric — sustained ROE above 15% signals a competitive moat. DuPont decomposition reveals whether high ROE comes from margins, turnover, or leverage.
roe.howToRead: min_roe=15 passes firms earning 15%+ on equity. At 20%+, the company likely has superior economics. But always diagnose the source: high margin (good), high turnover (good), or high leverage (dangerous).
roe.caution: Excessive debt shrinks equity, artificially inflating ROE — the fake high-ROE trap. Always verify with debt-to-equity. Capital-eroded firms (negative equity) can show positive ROE from dividing two negatives, which is meaningless.

piotroski_fscore.label: Piotroski F-Score
piotroski_fscore.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
piotroski_fscore.whenToUse: "Is this company's financial health improving across the board?" Piotroski's F-Score (2000) scores 9 binary financial criteria (profitability, leverage, operating efficiency). The definitive quality filter for value-stock screens.
piotroski_fscore.howToRead: min_score=7 passes firms scoring 7+ out of 9. Scores 0-3 indicate financial deterioration; 4-6 are neutral; 7-9 confirm broad-based improvement. Academically proven to boost returns when applied within low-PB stocks.
piotroski_fscore.caution: F-Score is based on annual financial statements, so it's inherently backward-looking and may lag by months. All 9 criteria carry equal weight, though in practice some (like ROA trend) matter more than others.

altman_zscore.label: Altman Z-Score
altman_zscore.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
altman_zscore.whenToUse: "Could this company go bankrupt within 2 years?" Altman Z-Score (1968) predicts insolvency. Summarizes financial safety in one number — a minimum safety net for value investing.
altman_zscore.howToRead: min_zscore=2.5 passes near-safe-zone firms (3.0+). Below 1.8 is distress zone; 1.8-3.0 is grey zone. Set 3.0+ for conservative screening.
altman_zscore.caution: Financial and service firms score structurally low — the model was designed for manufacturing. Non-manufacturers should use the modified Z''-Score, but this filter uses the original formula.

avg_trading_value.label: Average Trading Value
avg_trading_value.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
avg_trading_value.whenToUse: "Can you actually buy and sell this stock?" Average daily trading value — the liquidity benchmark. Without sufficient liquidity, slippage destroys backtested returns. Every strategy's first gate.
avg_trading_value.howToRead: min_value=1.5B (KRW) passes stocks with 20-day average trading value above 1.5 billion won. For US markets, adjust to $1M-$5M. Low liquidity = backtest lies.
avg_trading_value.caution: Earnings or thematic spikes cause temporary volume surges — use lookback=20+ days. Liquidity standards differ vastly by market (KOSDAQ small-cap 500M vs NASDAQ large-cap $100M).

roic.label: ROIC
roic.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
roic.whenToUse: "What after-tax operating return does the business generate on invested capital?" ROIC = NOPAT / Invested Capital. Greenblatt's Magic Formula core variable. Eliminates leverage effects to reveal true business economics.
roic.howToRead: min_roic=15 passes firms generating 15%+ after-tax operating return on invested capital. Must exceed WACC (typically 8-12%) to create shareholder value. At 20%+, strong competitive advantages are implied.
roic.caution: Invested capital calculation varies by analyst (goodwill inclusion, operating lease capitalization). Frequent acquirers get penalized by large goodwill balances. Standardize the calculation before comparing across firms.

analyst_revision_1m.label: Analyst Revision 1M
analyst_revision_1m.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
analyst_revision_1m.whenToUse: "Are analysts upgrading their view on this company?" One-month EPS revision rate. Often leads earnings surprises — a favorite tool of momentum investors.
analyst_revision_1m.howToRead: min_revision_pct=0 passes stocks with net upward revisions. Raise to 5 for clear upgrade trends. Higher values = rapidly improving Wall Street consensus.
analyst_revision_1m.caution: Small-cap stocks with 1-2 analyst coverage see extreme swings from a single opinion change. Post-upgrade price may already be priced in. Pair with PEG.

analyst_revision_3m.label: Analyst Revision 3M
analyst_revision_3m.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
analyst_revision_3m.whenToUse: "Is the consensus upgrade sustained, not just a one-month blip?" Three-month revision rate has less noise than 1-month, verifying trend persistence.
analyst_revision_3m.howToRead: min_revision_pct=0 passes stocks with positive 3-month net revisions. Combine with 1m revision to check if upgrades are "accelerating."
analyst_revision_3m.caution: Distorted right after earnings releases. Some quarters, forward guidance matters more. Exclude stocks with fewer than 3 analysts covering.

asset_turnover_ratio.label: Asset Turnover Ratio
asset_turnover_ratio.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
asset_turnover_ratio.whenToUse: "How efficiently does this company use its assets to generate revenue?" A key DuPont component — dissects ROE into margin, turnover, and leverage.
asset_turnover_ratio.howToRead: min_ratio=0.5 passes firms generating at least $0.50 revenue per $1 of assets. Retail often exceeds 2.0; utilities and financials are normally 0.1-0.3. Always compare within sector.
asset_turnover_ratio.caution: Asset-heavy firms (real estate, financials) are structurally low — never compare across sectors. Asset divestiture temporarily inflates the ratio.

book_to_market_ratio.label: Book to Market Ratio
book_to_market_ratio.desc: Book to Market Ratio fundamental condition
book_to_market_ratio.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
book_to_market_ratio.whenToUse: "How much is the market discounting this company vs. book value?" B/M ratio is the core Fama-French 3-factor variable. Higher = value stock; lower = growth premium.
book_to_market_ratio.howToRead: min_ratio=0.3 passes stocks where book value is at least 30% of market cap. Above 1.0 = "trading below book value" — classic value stock. 0.5-1.0 is mid-value zone.
book_to_market_ratio.caution: Inverse of PB ratio — may feel unfamiliar. IT/pharma with heavy intangibles (brands, patents) have low book values that understate true worth. Most reliable for financials and tangible-asset sectors.

buyback_yield_filter.label: Buyback Yield Filter
buyback_yield_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
buyback_yield_filter.whenToUse: "Is the company buying back its own stock?" Buyback yield signals management believes shares are undervalued. A key shareholder return metric alongside dividends.
buyback_yield_filter.howToRead: min_yield_pct=1.0 passes firms buying back at least 1% of market cap. Above 3% is very aggressive. Add to dividend yield for Total Shareholder Yield.
buyback_yield_filter.caution: Announcement vs. execution differ — many announce but don't follow through. "Defensive buybacks" that merely offset stock option dilution aren't real shareholder returns. Check net_share_issuance.

cash_conversion_ratio.label: Cash Conversion Ratio
cash_conversion_ratio.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
cash_conversion_ratio.whenToUse: "Is the company actually collecting cash from its profits?" Operating Cash Flow / Net Income. 1.0 = full cash collection; 0.5 = only half is cash. Directly measures earnings quality.
cash_conversion_ratio.howToRead: min_ratio=0.8 passes firms converting 80%+ of net income to cash. Above 1.0 is healthy; below 0.5 = "profits exist but cash doesn't" — a danger signal.
cash_conversion_ratio.caution: High-growth companies temporarily show low ratios due to working capital buildup. Also dips during heavy CAPEX periods. Use 3-5 year averages. Negative denominator (losses) distorts the ratio.

cashflow_to_debt_ratio.label: Cashflow to Debt Ratio
cashflow_to_debt_ratio.desc: Cashflow to Debt Ratio fundamental condition
cashflow_to_debt_ratio.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
cashflow_to_debt_ratio.whenToUse: "Can operating cash flow service the debt?" OCF / Total Debt. At 0.2, the company can repay all debt in 5 years at current pace. A core financial safety metric.
cashflow_to_debt_ratio.howToRead: min_ratio=0.2 passes firms covering 20%+ of total debt with annual OCF. Above 0.4 is solid; below 0.1 means heavy debt burden.
cashflow_to_debt_ratio.caution: Financials are structurally debt-heavy, so ratios are very low — apply different thresholds by sector. One-time cash inflows (asset sales) can temporarily inflate the ratio.

debt_service_coverage_ratio.label: Debt Service Coverage Ratio
debt_service_coverage_ratio.desc: Debt Service Coverage Ratio fundamental condition
debt_service_coverage_ratio.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
debt_service_coverage_ratio.whenToUse: "Can operating income cover interest and principal payments?" DSCR = EBIT / Total Debt Service. Banks use this as a core lending criterion. Below 1.0 = can't even cover interest.
debt_service_coverage_ratio.howToRead: min_ratio=1.2 passes firms with EBIT covering 1.2x their debt service. Above 1.5 is comfortable; 2.0+ is very strong. Banks typically require 1.25+.
debt_service_coverage_ratio.caution: EBIT can be inflated by one-time items. Short-term debt maturity concentration (refinancing risk) isn't captured. Check debt maturity structure alongside.

dividend_growth_5y.label: Dividend Growth 5Y
dividend_growth_5y.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
dividend_growth_5y.whenToUse: "Has this company consistently raised dividends?" The 5-year dividend growth rate is the backbone of Dividend Aristocrat strategies — sustained increases signal stable, predictable earnings.
dividend_growth_5y.howToRead: min_growth_pct=3 passes firms growing dividends at 3%+ annually. 7%+ beats inflation meaningfully; 10%+ marks aggressive dividend growers.
dividend_growth_5y.caution: Past growth doesn't guarantee future increases, especially in recessions. If payout ratio is already above 70%, growth headroom is exhausted. Pair with a payout ratio filter.

earnings_stability_score.label: Earnings Stability Score
earnings_stability_score.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
earnings_stability_score.whenToUse: "Are earnings predictable, or do they swing wildly?" The coefficient of variation (CV) of 5-year EPS. Low CV means stable, forecastable profits — a key criterion Benjamin Graham emphasized.
earnings_stability_score.howToRead: max_cv=0.35 passes firms with EPS variability under 35%. Below 0.2 is very stable (think utilities). Above 0.5 means erratic earnings typical of semiconductors or commodity producers.
earnings_stability_score.caution: Past stability doesn't immunize against disruption (regulation changes, new technology). Companies that swung from loss to profit will show extreme CV due to base effects. Check whether loss periods skew the calculation.

eps_cagr_3y.label: EPS CAGR 3Y
eps_cagr_3y.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
eps_cagr_3y.whenToUse: "Has this company grown earnings steadily over three years?" The 3-year EPS CAGR filters out one-year flukes and confirms sustained growth — essential for GARP (Growth at a Reasonable Price) screens.
eps_cagr_3y.howToRead: min_cagr_pct=5 passes firms with 5%+ annualized EPS growth. 10% is solid; 20%+ is high-growth territory. Pair with PEG to ensure you're not overpaying for that growth.
eps_cagr_3y.caution: Base effects are treacherous — a loss three years ago that flipped to profit creates astronomical CAGR. Always verify the starting EPS wasn't negative or abnormally depressed. Cross-check with revenue CAGR to confirm the growth source.

eps_growth_yoy.label: EPS Growth YoY
eps_growth_yoy.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
eps_growth_yoy.whenToUse: "Are this year's earnings higher than last year's?" Year-over-year EPS growth is the most intuitive growth metric and typically the first filter in earnings-momentum strategies.
eps_growth_yoy.howToRead: min_growth_pct=5 passes stocks with EPS up 5%+ YoY. At 20%, you're firmly in high-growth territory. Setting to 0 simply excludes companies with declining earnings.
eps_growth_yoy.caution: Single-year comparison is extremely vulnerable to base effects. A prior-year loss flipping to profit can show 1000%+ growth. Always combine with 3-year CAGR and check for one-time items (asset sales, tax refunds).

ev_to_ebitda_ratio.label: EV to EBITDA Ratio
ev_to_ebitda_ratio.desc: EV to EBITDA Ratio fundamental condition
ev_to_ebitda_ratio.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
ev_to_ebitda_ratio.whenToUse: "If I bought this entire company, how many years until the cash flow pays me back?" EV/EBITDA is the standard M&A valuation multiple. Unlike PE, it neutralizes debt structure and depreciation differences across industries.
ev_to_ebitda_ratio.howToRead: max_ratio=12 passes stocks trading at 12x EBITDA or below. KOSPI averages 8-10x; S&P 500 runs 12-15x. Sector norms vary widely — IT 20x+, utilities 8x, energy 5x.
ev_to_ebitda_ratio.caution: EBITDA ignores capex, so capital-intensive sectors (telecom, energy) look cheaper than they are on a free-cash-flow basis. Lease liabilities under IFRS 16 also shift the EV calculation significantly.

ev_to_sales_ratio.label: EV to Sales Ratio
ev_to_sales_ratio.desc: EV to Sales Ratio fundamental condition
ev_to_sales_ratio.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
ev_to_sales_ratio.whenToUse: "How do I value a company that doesn't yet have profits?" EV/Sales is the only usable valuation metric for pre-profit companies — essential for biotech, early-stage tech, and hypergrowth names.
ev_to_sales_ratio.howToRead: max_ratio=4 passes companies priced at 4x sales or less. Traditional manufacturing sits at 0.5-1.5x; SaaS companies can justify 5-15x if growth is strong. Always interpret alongside revenue growth rate.
ev_to_sales_ratio.caution: Low EV/Sales on a perpetually unprofitable company is not cheap — it may be "cheap for a reason." Pair with operating margin or FCF margin to filter out revenue-heavy, profit-absent businesses.

free_cash_flow_margin.label: Free Cash Flow Margin
free_cash_flow_margin.desc: Free Cash Flow Margin fundamental condition
free_cash_flow_margin.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
free_cash_flow_margin.whenToUse: "After all spending, how much real cash is left from each dollar of revenue?" FCF margin reveals profitability that accounting earnings can obscure. Cash flow doesn't lie — net income can.
free_cash_flow_margin.howToRead: min_margin_pct=5 passes firms converting 5%+ of revenue into free cash. IT/SaaS often exceeds 20%; manufacturing at 5% is respectable. Sector benchmarks vary widely.
free_cash_flow_margin.caution: Heavy capex periods (factory expansion, data-center buildout) temporarily depress FCF margin — that's investment, not weakness. Look at the 3-5 year trend. Filings may lag 1-2 months per quarter.

gross_margin.label: Gross Margin
gross_margin.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
gross_margin.whenToUse: "How much is left after subtracting cost of goods?" Gross margin is the most fundamental measure of a business's pricing power and competitive moat. One of Buffett's first-look metrics.
gross_margin.howToRead: min_margin_pct=20 passes companies retaining 20%+ of revenue after COGS. Software: 60-80%, pharma: 60-70%, retail: 25-35%, food processing: 20-30%. Always compare within the same sector.
gross_margin.caution: Cross-sector absolute comparisons are meaningless due to structural differences. Even within an industry, cost classification (COGS vs SGA) varies by company. Use peer-relative analysis.

gross_profitability.label: Gross Profitability
gross_profitability.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
gross_profitability.whenToUse: "How efficiently does this company turn its assets into gross profit?" Novy-Marx (2013) found that GP/Assets is a powerful quality factor — high-GP/A stocks outperform. The premier quality metric in academic factor models.
gross_profitability.howToRead: min_ratio=0.2 passes firms generating gross profit equal to 20%+ of total assets. Above 0.3 is very efficient. Used within value screens, it isolates "cheap and good" stocks.
gross_profitability.caution: Asset-light industries (tech, services) naturally score high while capital-heavy sectors (utilities, manufacturing) score low — not because they're worse businesses. For sector-neutral use, convert to within-sector percentile ranks.

interest_coverage_ratio.label: Interest Coverage Ratio
interest_coverage_ratio.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
interest_coverage_ratio.whenToUse: "Can this company cover its interest payments from operating profit?" ICR = EBIT / Interest Expense. Below 1.0 means the company can't even pay interest from operations. One of the most important metrics credit agencies examine.
interest_coverage_ratio.howToRead: min_ratio=3 passes firms earning 3x their interest costs. Above 5 is comfortable; below 1.5 is a warning. This is the financial safety net for any leveraged company.
interest_coverage_ratio.caution: In rising-rate environments, floating-rate debt can cause interest expense to spike, rapidly eroding ICR. Also verify that EBIT isn't inflated by one-time items. Check the debt maturity schedule for refinancing risk.

inventory_turnover_ratio.label: Inventory Turnover Ratio
inventory_turnover_ratio.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
inventory_turnover_ratio.whenToUse: "Is inventory selling quickly, or piling up in the warehouse?" High turnover means products are moving; declining turnover warns of demand weakness or overproduction — an early warning of margin compression.
inventory_turnover_ratio.howToRead: min_ratio=3 passes firms turning over inventory 3+ times per year. Retail: 8-12x, manufacturing: 4-8x, food: 12-20x. Norms vary enormously by industry.
inventory_turnover_ratio.caution: Service and software companies carry no inventory, making this metric irrelevant. Lean (just-in-time) inventory can inflate turnover while increasing supply-chain fragility. Focus on trend changes within the same sector.

net_debt_to_ebitda.label: Net Debt to EBITDA
net_debt_to_ebitda.desc: Net Debt to EBITDA fundamental condition
net_debt_to_ebitda.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
net_debt_to_ebitda.whenToUse: "How many years would it take to pay off all net debt from current cash earnings?" Net Debt/EBITDA is the standard leverage metric in credit analysis and M&A. It accounts for cash on hand, making it more realistic than gross debt ratios.
net_debt_to_ebitda.howToRead: max_ratio=3 passes firms that could pay off net debt in 3 years or less. Under 2x is healthy; above 5x is concerning. A negative ratio means cash exceeds debt (very strong balance sheet).
net_debt_to_ebitda.caution: EBITDA swells in boom times and shrinks in downturns, so cyclical firms look deceptively safe at peak earnings. Also check whether lease liabilities (IFRS 16) are included — they significantly change the numerator.

net_margin.label: Net Margin
net_margin.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
net_margin.whenToUse: "After everything — taxes, interest, all costs — what percentage of revenue remains as profit?" Net margin is the ultimate bottom-line profitability metric showing what shareholders truly earn per dollar of sales.
net_margin.howToRead: min_margin_pct=5 passes firms keeping 5%+ of revenue as net income. IT/SW: 20-30%, financials: 15-25%, retail: 2-5%, airlines: 3-8%. Norms are entirely sector-dependent.
net_margin.caution: Net income is the most susceptible to one-time items (asset sales, lawsuit settlements, tax windfalls). If operating margin is healthy but net margin is low, investigate non-operating charges (interest, FX losses). Use multi-year averages.

operating_margin.label: Operating Margin
operating_margin.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
operating_margin.whenToUse: "How profitable is the core business before financing and taxes?" Operating margin isolates the business's own efficiency, independent of capital structure. The key metric for comparing competitive positioning within an industry.
operating_margin.howToRead: min_margin_pct=10 passes firms retaining 10%+ of revenue as operating profit. IT/SW: 20-40%, pharma: 15-25%, retail: 3-8%, construction: 5-10%. Always benchmark against sector peers.
operating_margin.caution: Restructuring charges and asset impairments can distort operating income. Even within the same industry, different business models (own-brand vs contract manufacturing) create structural margin differences. Watch the trend — is it improving or deteriorating?

payout_ratio_filter.label: Payout Ratio Filter
payout_ratio_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
payout_ratio_filter.whenToUse: "Is the company paying out a sustainable share of earnings as dividends?" Payout ratio gauges dividend sustainability — too high means no reinvestment capacity; too low suggests weak shareholder return commitment.
payout_ratio_filter.howToRead: max_payout_pct=70 passes firms distributing 70% or less of net income. 40-60% is a balanced range. Over 100% means dividends exceed earnings — unsustainable without external financing. REITs legally require 90%+.
payout_ratio_filter.caution: A temporary earnings dip inflates payout ratio mechanically (denominator shrinks). Also, companies doing heavy buybacks may have low payout ratios but high total shareholder yield. Check shareholder_yield alongside.

price_to_tangible_book.label: Price to Tangible Book
price_to_tangible_book.desc: Price to Tangible Book fundamental condition
price_to_tangible_book.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
price_to_tangible_book.whenToUse: "What am I paying relative to hard, tangible assets — excluding goodwill and intangibles?" P/TBV strips out acquisition-inflated goodwill, giving a cleaner view of asset-based value. The most honest book-value metric for serial acquirers.
price_to_tangible_book.howToRead: max_ratio=3 passes stocks at 3x tangible book or below. Under 1.0 means the stock trades below its tangible liquidation value. P/TBV is the most relevant valuation metric for banks and financials.
price_to_tangible_book.caution: Companies whose core value is intangible (software, brands, patents) have minimal tangible book, making P/TBV meaninglessly high. This metric is powerful for asset-heavy sectors but misleading for asset-light businesses.

quality_score.label: Quality Score
quality_score.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
quality_score.whenToUse: "One composite score covering ROE, earnings stability, leverage, and more." A multi-factor quality score provides a single-number quality check when individually filtering on each metric is impractical.
quality_score.howToRead: min_score=0.5 passes the top half by quality. At 0.7, only the top 30%; at 0.9, top 10%. Represents the quality dimension in multi-factor models as a single summary value.
quality_score.caution: The components and weights inside any quality score vary by implementation — always understand the recipe before trusting the output. For full transparency, consider building your own from ROE, FCF margin, and F-Score.

receivables_turnover_ratio.label: Receivables Turnover Ratio
receivables_turnover_ratio.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
receivables_turnover_ratio.whenToUse: "How fast does this company collect what it's owed?" High receivables turnover means cash is coming in quickly. A declining ratio warns that revenue may be booked on paper but not actually collected — a credit-risk signal.
receivables_turnover_ratio.howToRead: min_ratio=4 passes firms collecting receivables 4+ times per year (~90-day cycle). Above 8 means sub-45-day collection. Retail and cash-based businesses are naturally very high; B2B and construction run low.
receivables_turnover_ratio.caution: Normal ranges are entirely sector-specific — absolute comparison across industries is invalid. Payment terms (Net 30, Net 60) create structural differences. Focus on changes in the trend, not the level.

revenue_cagr_3y.label: Revenue CAGR 3Y
revenue_cagr_3y.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
revenue_cagr_3y.whenToUse: "Has revenue grown steadily over three years?" Revenue CAGR is harder to manipulate than EPS and less prone to base-effect distortions. The most reliable proof that the business is genuinely expanding.
revenue_cagr_3y.howToRead: min_cagr_pct=5 passes firms growing revenue at 5%+ annually. 10% is solid; 20%+ is high growth. Pair with EPS CAGR to verify whether revenue growth is translating to profit growth.
revenue_cagr_3y.caution: M&A-driven revenue jumps inflate CAGR without representing organic growth. Check if acquisitions distort the number. Also compare against asset growth to detect dilutive expansion.

revenue_growth_yoy.label: Revenue Growth YoY
revenue_growth_yoy.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
revenue_growth_yoy.whenToUse: "Did revenue increase this year versus last?" Year-over-year revenue growth is the simplest growth indicator. Revenue is harder to fabricate than earnings, making it the most trustworthy first evidence of real growth.
revenue_growth_yoy.howToRead: min_growth_pct=5 passes stocks with 5%+ YoY revenue growth. Setting to 0 merely excludes shrinking businesses. At 20%+ you are in high-growth territory. Compare against sector average for relative positioning.
revenue_growth_yoy.caution: Single-year comparisons are vulnerable to base effects — a COVID-depressed prior year inflates this year's growth. Cross-reference with 3-year CAGR. FX fluctuations also affect revenue for multinational companies.

revenue_stability_score.label: Revenue Stability Score
revenue_stability_score.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
revenue_stability_score.whenToUse: "Is revenue predictable year to year, or does it swing with the cycle?" Low revenue CV indicates stable, recession-resistant business models like subscriptions, utilities, and consumer staples.
revenue_stability_score.howToRead: max_cv=0.25 passes firms with revenue variability under 25% over 5 years. Below 0.1 is extremely stable (utilities, telecom). Above 0.5 indicates highly cyclical exposure (semiconductors, commodities).
revenue_stability_score.caution: Stable revenue doesn't guarantee growth — it can mean stagnation. If you are seeking growth stocks, this filter works against you. Also, business-model pivots (entering new markets) invalidate historical stability patterns.

shareholder_yield_filter.label: Shareholder Yield Filter
shareholder_yield_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
shareholder_yield_filter.whenToUse: "What is the total cash return to shareholders — dividends, buybacks, and debt paydown combined?" Mebane Faber's Shareholder Yield captures the full picture of capital return that dividend yield alone misses.
shareholder_yield_filter.howToRead: min_yield_pct=2 passes firms returning 2%+ of market cap to shareholders annually. At 5%+, the return is very aggressive. Catches buyback-heavy, low-dividend companies that dividend screens miss.
shareholder_yield_filter.caution: Treasury stock (buybacks held, not cancelled) is not true return. Debt paydown inclusion is debatable — routine refinancing counts as shareholder yield under some definitions. Decompose the components to verify real return.

roce_filter.label: ROCE Filter
roce_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
roce_filter.whenToUse: "What return is the business generating on all invested capital — both equity and debt?" ROCE = EBIT / Capital Employed. Measures how efficiently a firm deploys the total capital entrusted to it. A Buffett favorite.
roce_filter.howToRead: min_roce_pct=10 passes firms earning 10%+ on capital employed. Above 15% is strong; 20%+ suggests durable competitive advantage (moat). Must exceed WACC (typically 8-12%) to be value-creative.
roce_filter.caution: Capital employed definitions vary among analysts (include goodwill or not, capitalize leases or not). Serial acquirers accumulate goodwill that bloats capital and depresses ROCE. Calculate organic ROCE separately for clarity.

roa_filter.label: ROA Filter
roa_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
roa_filter.whenToUse: "How efficiently does this company generate profit from its total asset base?" ROA strips out leverage effects, showing pure asset-utilization efficiency. More useful than ROE for cross-industry comparison.
roa_filter.howToRead: min_roa_pct=5 passes firms earning 5%+ on total assets. IT/SW: 10-20%, retail: 5-10%, banking: 0.5-1.5%, utilities: 2-5%. The huge variation makes sector benchmarking essential.
roa_filter.caution: Asset-heavy industries (banking, insurance) have structurally low ROA (0.5-1.5%) by design, not incompetence. Apply sector-specific thresholds. A large gap between ROE and ROA signals heavy reliance on leverage.

overnight_return_filter.label: Overnight Return
overnight_return_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
overnight_return_filter.whenToUse: "Was the overnight gap positive?" The prior close to current open return reflects after-hours news, earnings, and foreign market movements. Some research suggests a significant portion of equity returns occurs overnight rather than intraday.
overnight_return_filter.howToRead: min_overnight_return_pct=0 passes stocks that gapped up at the open. At 1% the overnight move is meaningful. Negative values filter for gap-downs, useful for overnight risk analysis.
overnight_return_filter.caution: Overnight returns are extremely noisy day-to-day and driven by US futures/Asian market spillover. Predicting next-day gaps is nearly impossible. More useful for portfolio overnight-risk profiling than for screening.

distance_from_52w_low.label: Distance From 52W Low
distance_from_52w_low.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
distance_from_52w_low.whenToUse: "How far has this stock bounced from its 52-week low?" Measures recovery from the bottom. Used for oversold-bounce or "confirmed bottom" entry strategies.
distance_from_52w_low.howToRead: max_distance_pct=30 passes stocks still within 30% of their 52-week low — still beaten down. Raise to 100 to include stocks that already doubled. Adjust range by strategy purpose.
distance_from_52w_low.caution: Stocks near the 52-week low are usually cheap for a reason (problems), not because they're bargains. Value trap risk is high. Always pair with fundamental filters (FCF, debt).

distance_from_200d_high.label: Distance From 200D High
distance_from_200d_high.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
distance_from_200d_high.whenToUse: "How far has this stock fallen from its 200-day high?" Filters out stocks that dropped too far, or conversely keeps only momentum stocks near their highs.
distance_from_200d_high.howToRead: max_distance_pct=15 passes stocks within 15% of their 200-day high. Lower to 5 for near-highs only; raise to 30 to include significantly pulled-back stocks.
distance_from_200d_high.caution: Near the high doesn't always mean good — could be overbought. Far from the high could mean further decline ahead. Set direction based on strategy purpose (momentum vs. contrarian).

gap_up_breakaway.label: Gap Up Breakaway
gap_up_breakaway.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
gap_up_breakaway.whenToUse: "Did price gap up and hold — signaling the start of a new uptrend?" A breakaway gap marks the beginning of a fresh trend, especially when accompanied by heavy volume. Connects with PEAD after earnings surprises.
gap_up_breakaway.howToRead: min_gap_pct=1 passes stocks opening 1%+ above the prior close. At 3%, the gap is decisive. Post-earnings surprise gaps tied to PEAD often carry momentum for weeks.
gap_up_breakaway.caution: Not every gap-up is breakaway — exhaustion gaps near tops look identical. Declining volume after the gap signals insufficient follow-through buying. Confirm the gap holds (isn't filled) over 1-2 days.

gap_down_exhaustion.label: Gap Down Exhaustion
gap_down_exhaustion.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
gap_down_exhaustion.whenToUse: "After a panic gap-down, did the stock recover to close higher — signaling selling exhaustion?" A large gap-down followed by a bullish close suggests panic sellers are depleted. A short-term contrarian reversal pattern.
gap_down_exhaustion.howToRead: min_gap_down_pct=2 passes stocks that opened 2%+ below the prior close but finished the day positive. At 5%, you're filtering for extreme panic-recovery events only.
gap_down_exhaustion.caution: This is a "catching falling knives" pattern — inherently dangerous. Verify whether the gap-down cause (earnings miss, bad news) is temporary or structural. Structural bad news leads to continued decline after any dead-cat bounce.

opening_range_breakout.label: Opening Range Breakout
opening_range_breakout.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
opening_range_breakout.whenToUse: "Did price break above the early-session range?" Opening Range Breakout is a classic day-trading strategy where breaking the initial price range signals momentum continuation in that direction.
opening_range_breakout.howToRead: direction=up passes stocks that broke above their opening range. On daily bars, this approximates breaking the prior day's high. True intraday ORB (15-30 min range) requires tick data.
opening_range_breakout.caution: Volatile stocks routinely break the opening range in both directions during a single session. Daily-bar screening can only approximate this inherently intraday signal. Precision is limited outside real-time data.

pivot_point_breakout.label: Pivot Point Breakout
pivot_point_breakout.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
pivot_point_breakout.whenToUse: "Has price moved above yesterday's pivot point?" Pivot points (average of prior high, low, close) are a self-fulfilling day-trading reference that many floor traders and algorithms use for intraday support/resistance.
pivot_point_breakout.howToRead: direction=up passes stocks trading above their pivot point. R1 and R2 levels represent increasing resistance zones above the pivot. Widely watched enough to create real supply/demand at these calculated levels.
pivot_point_breakout.caution: Because so many traders use pivots, reversals at pivot levels are common — the signal both attracts and repels price. On daily-bar screening, intraday pivot precision is lost. Best suited for real-time trading.

month_of_year_seasonality.label: Month Of Year Seasonality
month_of_year_seasonality.desc: Month Of Year Seasonality event/seasonality condition
month_of_year_seasonality.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
month_of_year_seasonality.whenToUse: "Does this stock show a repeating pattern of strong performance in a specific month?" Tests calendar anomalies like the January Effect and Sell in May. Based on decades of academic seasonal-pattern research.
month_of_year_seasonality.howToRead: target_month=1 with min_avg_return_pct=0 passes stocks whose average January return is positive. Change the month number to test any month. For Sell in May, examine months 5-10.
month_of_year_seasonality.caution: Monthly seasonality has very small sample sizes (12 data points per year) and most effects disappear after transaction costs. Extremely high over-optimization risk. Use only as a secondary reference, never as a primary strategy driver.

turn_of_month_effect.label: Turn Of Month
turn_of_month_effect.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
turn_of_month_effect.whenToUse: "Does this stock benefit from the well-documented end-of-month/start-of-month seasonal pattern?" The Turn-of-Month effect (last 3 + first 3 days) is among the most statistically robust calendar anomalies, linked to payroll and pension fund inflows.
turn_of_month_effect.howToRead: window_days=3 passes stocks with positive average returns in the turn-of-month window. This effect has stronger academic support than day-of-week effects and appears across many global markets.
turn_of_month_effect.caution: Even if the effect is real, it is a market-wide phenomenon — using it to select individual stocks adds limited value. Transaction costs erode the already-thin alpha for individual investors. Useful only as a market-timing reference.

day_of_week_seasonality.label: Day-of-Week Seasonality
day_of_week_seasonality.desc: Filters stocks that historically perform better on a selected weekday.
day_of_week_seasonality.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
day_of_week_seasonality.whenToUse: "Do certain stocks consistently perform better on specific weekdays?" Tests the Day-of-Week Effect — the classic calendar anomaly of weak Mondays and strong Fridays.
day_of_week_seasonality.howToRead: target_weekday=0 (Monday), min_avg_return_pct=0 passes stocks with positive Monday average returns. For Friday test: target_weekday=4. Academically, this effect is weakening.
day_of_week_seasonality.caution: Transaction costs and slippage eliminate most day-of-week alpha. High overfitting risk — a specific day's outperformance may be pure chance. Use as reference only, never as primary strategy.

net_share_issuance_filter.label: Net Share Issuance Filter
net_share_issuance_filter.desc: Limits dilution by filtering companies issuing too many new shares.
net_share_issuance_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
net_share_issuance_filter.whenToUse: "Is this company diluting shareholders by issuing new stock?" Pontiff & Woodgate (2008) confirmed that high net share issuance predicts poor future returns. A quality/governance filter against equity dilution.
net_share_issuance_filter.howToRead: max_issuance_pct=1 passes firms with net issuance under 1% of shares outstanding. Negative values indicate net buybacks (positive signal). Above 5% suggests significant dilution from secondary offerings or convertible bonds.
net_share_issuance_filter.caution: Stock-based compensation in tech companies counts as issuance, making blanket cutoffs tricky. Distinguish between dilutive issuance (secondaries) and defensive buybacks that merely offset options dilution. Check net issuance vs. buyback_yield together.

insider_net_buying.label: Insider Net Buying
insider_net_buying.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
insider_net_buying.whenToUse: "Are executives buying their own company's stock with personal money?" Insiders know the business best — when they buy, it's a bullish signal. SEC mandates public disclosure of insider transactions.
insider_net_buying.howToRead: min_net_buying_pct=0 passes stocks with more insider buying than selling. Above 1% of float is meaningful. There's only one reason insiders buy (they think it's undervalued); there are many reasons they sell (taxes, diversification).
insider_net_buying.caution: "Insider buying has one reason; selling has a hundred" — never interpret selling alone as bearish. Most insider sales are mechanical (tax payments on exercised options). Focus exclusively on insider purchases.

short_float_pct_filter.label: Short Float % Filter
short_float_pct_filter.desc: Limits candidates by short interest as a percentage of float.
short_float_pct_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
short_float_pct_filter.whenToUse: "What fraction of tradable shares are currently shorted?" High short interest signals bearish consensus but also short-squeeze potential. A sentiment indicator that cuts both ways.
short_float_pct_filter.howToRead: max_short_float_pct=15 excludes stocks with more than 15% of float shorted. Inversely, setting a min threshold finds squeeze candidates. Above 20% is unusually high short interest.
short_float_pct_filter.caution: Short interest data is published biweekly (US) and is already stale on release. High short interest can be non-directional (hedging, pairs trading, market-making). Context matters — don't assume all shorts are bearish bets.

short_interest_ratio_filter.label: Short Interest Ratio Filter
short_interest_ratio_filter.desc: Filters by days-to-cover level from short interest.
short_interest_ratio_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
short_interest_ratio_filter.whenToUse: "How many days would it take for shorts to cover at average volume?" Days-to-cover combines short interest with liquidity — high values mean shorts are trapped if the stock rallies, amplifying squeeze dynamics.
short_interest_ratio_filter.howToRead: max_ratio=5 passes stocks where shorts can cover in 5 days or less. Above 10 days, a squeeze is structurally plausible. Setting a min threshold specifically hunts for squeeze setups.
short_interest_ratio_filter.caution: High days-to-cover does not guarantee a squeeze — a catalyst is required to force covering. Data is biweekly and potentially stale. Shorts may have already begun covering by the time you see the report.

earnings_surprise_filter.label: Earnings Surprise Filter
earnings_surprise_filter.desc: Filters stocks with positive earnings surprise vs consensus.
earnings_surprise_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
earnings_surprise_filter.whenToUse: "Did the latest quarter beat expectations?" Earnings surprises drive the Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift (PEAD) — one of the most robust anomalies in academic finance (Bernard & Thomas, 1989).
earnings_surprise_filter.howToRead: min_surprise_pct=0 passes stocks that beat consensus. At 5, only 5%+ beats qualify. PEAD suggests price continues drifting in the surprise direction for 60-90 days post-announcement.
earnings_surprise_filter.caution: Stocks often gap up immediately on surprise, making entry timing tricky. A "sell the news" reaction can also occur. Combining with post-announcement price action (gap_up) improves signal quality.

post_earnings_drift.label: Post Earnings Drift
post_earnings_drift.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
post_earnings_drift.whenToUse: "Does price keep drifting in the direction of a positive earnings surprise?" PEAD (Bernard & Thomas, 1989) is one of the most robust market anomalies — the market digests earnings news slowly, creating exploitable drift for 60-90 days.
post_earnings_drift.howToRead: min_return_pct=0 passes stocks with positive post-announcement returns. PEAD is stronger for larger surprises and persists longer in small-caps with lower analyst coverage.
post_earnings_drift.caution: Institutional awareness of PEAD has grown, weakening the effect. Large post-earnings gaps may already price in most of the drift. The highest-probability entries are within 2-3 days of the announcement.

pre_earnings_drift.label: Pre Earnings Drift
pre_earnings_drift.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
pre_earnings_drift.whenToUse: "Is the stock rising ahead of its earnings announcement — suggesting the market anticipates a beat?" Pre-announcement drift can reflect informed expectations or, in some cases, information leakage.
pre_earnings_drift.howToRead: min_return_pct=0 passes stocks with positive returns in the pre-announcement window. Strong pre-earnings momentum often indicates the market is pricing in a positive surprise.
pre_earnings_drift.caution: "Buy the rumor, sell the news" — stocks that rally into earnings often sell off on the actual report even if results are good. Also, abnormal pre-earnings moves may attract regulatory scrutiny. Don't over-rely on this pattern.

accruals_ratio.label: Accruals Ratio
accruals_ratio.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
accruals_ratio.whenToUse: "Are these profits real, or just accounting entries?" Sloan(1996) discovered the accrual anomaly — high accrual firms underperform. A quality filter that verifies earnings authenticity.
accruals_ratio.howToRead: max_ratio=0.1 passes firms with accruals below 10% of total assets. Lower values mean more cash-based earnings. Near zero means "genuinely making money."
accruals_ratio.caution: High accruals aren't always bad — fast-growing companies naturally see rising receivables/inventory. Consider industry norms. Cross-check with FCF margin.

asset_growth_rate.label: Asset Growth Rate
asset_growth_rate.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
asset_growth_rate.whenToUse: "Is this company growing its assets too fast?" Cooper et al. (2008) found high asset-growth firms underperform. A quality filter catching overinvestment and reckless acquisitions.
asset_growth_rate.howToRead: max_growth_pct=15 passes firms with YoY total asset growth under 15%. 0-10% is healthy; 30%+ raises red flags for large acquisitions or equity offerings.
asset_growth_rate.caution: High asset growth from R&D or capacity expansion can be positive. Don't apply a blanket cutoff — consider industry CAPEX cycles. Semiconductors and biotech fluctuate heavily.

momentum_12_1.label: Momentum 12-1
momentum_12_1.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
momentum_12_1.whenToUse: "The academically most-validated momentum factor." Returns over months 2-12 (skipping the most recent month to avoid short-term reversal). Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) established this as the gold standard of momentum measurement.
momentum_12_1.howToRead: min_return_pct=20 passes stocks up 20%+ over the 11-month window (12 months minus the most recent 1). The skip_recent=1 is critical — including the last month degrades performance due to the mean-reversion effect.
momentum_12_1.caution: Momentum crashes are real — in 2009's sharp rebound, momentum stocks collapsed simultaneously. Past 12-month winners may be overbought. Always pair with volatility or MDD risk filters to manage crash exposure.

volatility_n_day.label: Volatility N Day
volatility_n_day.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
