volatility_n_day.whenToUse: "Is this stock's total volatility within my risk budget?" Annualized N-day volatility is the most fundamental risk metric and the primary input for position sizing. Every portfolio management framework starts here.
volatility_n_day.howToRead: max_annualized_vol_pct=25 passes stocks with annualized volatility under 25%. S&P 500 long-term average is 15-18%. Under 20% is low-vol; above 40% is high-vol. Use inversely for position sizing (higher vol = smaller position).
volatility_n_day.caution: Historical volatility does not predict future volatility — the 2018 vol shock proved that calm periods can end abruptly. Total vol counts up-moves as risk; for a loss-only measure, use downside volatility instead.

distance_from_52w_high.label: Distance From 52W High
distance_from_52w_high.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
distance_from_52w_high.whenToUse: "How close is this stock to its 52-week high?" Near-52w-high stocks carry strong momentum. George & Hwang (2004) showed this strategy is more stable than traditional momentum.
distance_from_52w_high.howToRead: max_distance_pct=10 passes stocks within 10% of their 52-week high. At 5%, stocks are near new highs. One of the simplest and most intuitive momentum filters.
distance_from_52w_high.caution: If the 52-week high was months ago and the stock is flat since, it's stalled — not momentum. Check recency of the high. Post-spike stocks near their high may already be too late.

relative_strength_vs_benchmark.label: Relative Strength Vs Benchmark
relative_strength_vs_benchmark.desc: Relative Strength Vs Benchmark trend/momentum condition
relative_strength_vs_benchmark.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
relative_strength_vs_benchmark.whenToUse: "Is this stock outperforming the market?" Relative strength measures excess returns over a benchmark. Stocks beating the index show alpha — the market is falling but this stock is holding or rising.
relative_strength_vs_benchmark.howToRead: min_excess_return_pct=5 passes stocks outperforming the benchmark by 5%+ over 63 days (3 months). At 10%, only clear winners qualify. This is relative, not absolute — even in a down market, leaders are identified.
relative_strength_vs_benchmark.caution: High relative strength stocks may already be extended — chasing them risks buying the top. In market sell-offs, defensive sectors (utilities, staples) naturally rank first, creating sector concentration bias.

adx_trend_strength.label: ADX Trend Strength
adx_trend_strength.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
adx_trend_strength.whenToUse: "Is there actually a trend, or is it sideways?" ADX measures trend strength — not direction. Essential pre-check: "Is a trend-following strategy even viable right now?"
adx_trend_strength.howToRead: min_adx=25 passes stocks with clear trends. Below 15 = sideways; 25-50 = moderate to strong; 50+ = extremely strong. Set di_direction=up to filter for uptrends only.
adx_trend_strength.caution: ADX is lagging — it stays high even after trends reverse. High ADX doesn't reveal direction. Always pair with DI+/DI- directional filters.

ma_ribbon_alignment.label: MA Ribbon Alignment
ma_ribbon_alignment.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
ma_ribbon_alignment.whenToUse: "Are all timeframes — short, medium, and long — aligned in the same direction?" When 20 > 50 > 200 MA, every timeframe confirms bullish consensus. Maximum trend confidence comes from full ribbon alignment.
ma_ribbon_alignment.howToRead: Passes when 20MA > 50MA > 200MA (perfect bullish order). The reverse (20<50<200) is full bearish alignment. MAs converging signals an impending trend change. Breakdown of alignment is an exit signal.
ma_ribbon_alignment.caution: Full alignment is achieved only after significant price appreciation — entries may be late. Once established, alignment persists for long stretches, yielding few new signals. Catching the moment alignment first completes is the key.

golden_cross_50_200.label: Golden Cross 50/200
golden_cross_50_200.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
golden_cross_50_200.whenToUse: "Is a long-term trend reversal underway?" The 50-day MA crossing above the 200-day MA — the golden cross — is the single most widely watched trend-transition signal by institutions and financial media.
golden_cross_50_200.howToRead: lookback_days=5 passes stocks where the golden cross occurred within 5 days. These events are rare; widening to 10-20 days increases matches. The self-fulfilling attention the signal attracts can add short-term momentum.
golden_cross_50_200.caution: The golden cross is a lagging signal — by the time it forms, price has typically recovered 30-40% from its bottom (as in the 2020 V-shaped recovery). Entry prices may already be elevated.

death_cross_50_200.label: Death Cross 50/200
death_cross_50_200.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
death_cross_50_200.whenToUse: "Is a long-term downtrend beginning?" The 50-day MA crossing below the 200-day MA — a widely watched warning of trend deterioration. Used for risk management or short entry timing.
death_cross_50_200.howToRead: lookback_days=5 passes stocks where death cross occurred within 5 days. Rare signal, so results may be thin. Extend to 10-20 for wider capture.
death_cross_50_200.caution: Classic lagging signal — the actual decline is largely over by the time it appears. In V-shaped recoveries (like 2020 COVID), it triggers sells at the bottom. Always pair with other confirmation.

donchian_channel_breakout.label: Donchian Channel Breakout
donchian_channel_breakout.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
donchian_channel_breakout.whenToUse: "Has price broken the N-day high — the classic Turtle Trading signal?" Richard Dennis's legendary system used 20-day channel breakouts as the primary trend-following entry rule.
donchian_channel_breakout.howToRead: lookback_days=20 passes stocks breaking above their 20-day high. The original Turtle system used 20 (short-term) and 55 (long-term). Longer periods yield fewer but higher-conviction signals.
donchian_channel_breakout.caution: In range-bound markets, price grazes the upper channel and reverts — false breakouts are common. The Turtle system's win rate was below 40%; profits came from riding large trends. A disciplined stop-loss is essential.

keltner_channel_breakout.label: Keltner Channel Breakout
keltner_channel_breakout.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
keltner_channel_breakout.whenToUse: "Has price broken above the ATR-based volatility channel?" The Keltner Channel (EMA +/- ATR multiple) reacts more uniformly to spikes than Bollinger Bands. A breakout above the upper channel signals strong directional momentum.
keltner_channel_breakout.howToRead: atr_multiplier=2 passes stocks breaking above EMA + 2x ATR. At 1.5, signals are more frequent; at 3.0, only extreme breakouts qualify. Combining with BB creates the well-known TTM Squeeze confirmation.
keltner_channel_breakout.caution: Like Bollinger breakouts, false signals are common without volume confirmation. The Keltner + BB squeeze combo (price exits Keltner while BB is inside it) is popular but still needs directional validation.

parabolic_sar_flip.label: Parabolic SAR Flip
parabolic_sar_flip.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
parabolic_sar_flip.whenToUse: "Has the Parabolic SAR flipped to below price, signaling a shift from downtrend to uptrend?" Developed by Welles Wilder, SAR serves as both a trend-following entry and a trailing stop-loss system.
parabolic_sar_flip.howToRead: lookback_days=5 passes stocks where SAR flipped below price (bullish) within 5 days. af_step=0.02 is standard; af_max=0.2 caps acceleration. Higher af_max makes SAR cling tighter to price.
parabolic_sar_flip.caution: SAR excels in trending markets but produces rapid flip-flops in sideways conditions. Restrict usage to ADX 25+ environments. Since SAR provides only a single value, always cross-reference with at least one other indicator.

linear_regression_slope_filter.label: Linear Regression Slope
linear_regression_slope_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
linear_regression_slope_filter.whenToUse: "Is the statistical price trend genuinely upward?" The regression slope in price units is positive when the trend is rising. Less ambiguous than moving average direction and more comparable across stocks when normalized.
linear_regression_slope_filter.howToRead: min_slope=0 passes stocks with a positive 60-day regression slope. Because the unit is in price (dollars or won), direct cross-stock comparison requires normalization to percentage terms.
linear_regression_slope_filter.caution: Absolute slope scales with price level — a $100 stock and a $10 stock with identical percentage trends have 10x different slopes. Use return-based slope or pair with R-squared and angle for proper context.

linear_regression_angle_filter.label: Linear Regression Angle
linear_regression_angle_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
linear_regression_angle_filter.whenToUse: "Is the price trend line sloping upward, and how steeply?" Linear regression angle provides a mathematically precise trend direction measure — more rigorous than eyeballing moving averages.
linear_regression_angle_filter.howToRead: min_angle_deg=0 passes stocks with a positive (upward-sloping) 60-day regression line. 30 degrees is a brisk rise; 45 degrees is very steep. The angle is intuitive but depends on the Y-axis scale.
linear_regression_angle_filter.caution: Angle values depend on price units, so the same return can produce different angles for a $10 stock vs a $500 stock. Prefer relative comparison over absolute thresholds. Always combine with R-squared to avoid noisy trends.

linear_regression_r2_filter.label: Linear Regression R2
linear_regression_r2_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
linear_regression_r2_filter.whenToUse: "How cleanly is price following a straight-line trend?" High R-squared means price moves are largely explained by a linear trend (low noise). This measures trend quality — essential before trusting slope or angle signals.
linear_regression_r2_filter.howToRead: min_r2=0.5 passes stocks where 50%+ of price movement is explained by the trend. Above 0.7 is a very clean trend. Below 0.3 means noise dominates over trend.
linear_regression_r2_filter.caution: High R-squared with a negative slope means the stock is declining cleanly — always pair with slope or angle direction. Sudden large moves can artificially inflate R-squared, so ensure the lookback period (60+ days) is long enough.

beta_to_benchmark.label: Beta to Benchmark
beta_to_benchmark.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
beta_to_benchmark.whenToUse: "How much does this stock drop when the market drops 1%?" Beta measures market sensitivity. Core tool for adjusting portfolio market risk — low beta for defense, high for offense.
beta_to_benchmark.howToRead: max_beta=1.2 excludes stocks that swing more than 1.2x the market. Lower to 0.8 for defensive-only stocks. lookback=252 (1 year) gives more stable estimates.
beta_to_benchmark.caution: Beta is backward-looking and changes completely during regime shifts (rate hikes, wars). Low beta doesn't always win — it means lower returns in bull markets too. Adjust by market phase.

correlation_to_benchmark.label: Correlation to Benchmark
correlation_to_benchmark.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
correlation_to_benchmark.whenToUse: "How much does this stock move with the market?" Low correlation maximizes portfolio diversification. The core of defending against market-wide crashes.
correlation_to_benchmark.howToRead: max_corr=0.8 passes stocks with correlation below 0.8 to benchmark. Lower to 0.5 for significantly independent stocks. Longer lookback = more stable but may miss recent changes.
correlation_to_benchmark.caution: Correlations converge toward 1.0 during market crises (correlation breakdown). Stocks that seem uncorrelated in normal times may all crash together when it matters most. Stress-test separately.

support_retest_signal.label: Support Retest Signal
support_retest_signal.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
support_retest_signal.whenToUse: "Is price bouncing off a previous low — confirming support?" A price revisiting a prior low and holding it suggests a double-bottom pattern, one of the most trusted reversal signals in classical chart analysis.
support_retest_signal.howToRead: support_lookback=40 with tolerance_pct=1 passes stocks that touched within 1% of a 40-day low and bounced. When the same level holds 2-3 times, it becomes strong confirmed support.
support_retest_signal.caution: If the support level breaks, losses accelerate — always set a stop just below the tested support. What appears as support may simply be a temporary pause in a downtrend. Combine with trend-direction filters.

resistance_retest_signal.label: Resistance Retest Signal
resistance_retest_signal.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
resistance_retest_signal.whenToUse: "Has former resistance flipped to support — confirming the breakout was genuine?" When price pulls back to an old resistance level and bounces, it is the classic role-reversal pattern — one of the highest-confidence technical entries.
resistance_retest_signal.howToRead: resistance_lookback=40 with tolerance_pct=1 passes stocks that broke out above 40-day resistance, pulled back to within 1% of that level, and held. This is a textbook pullback-entry setup.
resistance_retest_signal.caution: If the pullback breaks through the old resistance, the breakout has failed — the most dangerous setup to be caught in. Always set a stop-loss just below the retest level. Thicker former resistance zones make more reliable support.

downside_volatility_filter.label: Downside Volatility
downside_volatility_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
downside_volatility_filter.whenToUse: "How badly does this stock fall when it drops?" Downside volatility isolates negative moves only. Standard volatility includes rallies, but investors really only worry about losses. This is the denominator of the Sortino ratio.
downside_volatility_filter.howToRead: max_downside_vol_pct=20 passes stocks with annualized downside vol under 20%. Lowering to 15 keeps only the most stable names. More precise than total volatility for loss-averse investors.
downside_volatility_filter.caution: Low past downside vol can't predict structural shocks (lawsuits, regulatory changes). In bull markets, downside vol is naturally compressed, inflating its apparent safety. Include bear-market data for a realistic picture.

semivariance_filter.label: Semivariance
semivariance_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
semivariance_filter.whenToUse: "How severe is the downside dispersion in this stock's returns?" Semivariance measures variance on loss days only — the purest statistical quantification of downside risk and the denominator of the Sortino ratio.
semivariance_filter.howToRead: max_semivariance=0.0004 passes stocks with daily downside variance under 0.0004 (~10% annualized downside vol). At 0.0001, only very stable names pass (~5% annualized). At 0.001, risk tolerance is high.
semivariance_filter.caution: The raw number is not intuitive — convert to annualized downside volatility (sqrt(semivariance x 252)) for readability. If downside_volatility_filter gives the same information more clearly, prefer that one.

rolling_sharpe_filter.label: Rolling Sharpe
rolling_sharpe_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
rolling_sharpe_filter.whenToUse: "How much return am I getting per unit of risk?" The Sharpe ratio is the universal risk-adjusted performance metric. Above 1.0 is respectable; above 2.0 is excellent. Below 0 means worse than holding risk-free assets.
rolling_sharpe_filter.howToRead: min_sharpe=1.0 passes stocks with 60-day rolling Sharpe at or above 1.0 (annualized: 1% excess return per 1% volatility). Higher is better. The go-to metric for comparing risk-efficiency across assets.
rolling_sharpe_filter.caution: Sharpe penalizes upside volatility equally to downside — a stock that rockets upward gets no credit. For asymmetric return profiles, Sortino is superior. Also, in sustained bull markets, nearly everything scores well.

rolling_sortino_filter.label: Rolling Sortino
rolling_sortino_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
rolling_sortino_filter.whenToUse: "How much return am I getting per unit of downside risk only?" Sortino is Sharpe with a fairer denominator — only harmful (downside) volatility is penalized. More aligned with what investors actually worry about.
rolling_sortino_filter.howToRead: min_sortino=1.0 passes stocks with 60-day rolling Sortino at 1.0+. Always higher than Sharpe (smaller denominator). Above 2.0 means excellent downside-adjusted performance.
rolling_sortino_filter.caution: Same bull-market inflation problem as Sharpe — use a lookback that includes at least one drawdown period (120+ days). The result also depends on the MAR (minimum acceptable return) — 0% or the risk-free rate — so confirm the calculation basis.

ulcer_index_filter.label: Ulcer Index
ulcer_index_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
ulcer_index_filter.whenToUse: "How painful have recent drawdowns been — in both depth and duration?" The Ulcer Index captures what MDD misses: the duration of underwater periods. Named for the stress investors feel during prolonged losses.
ulcer_index_filter.howToRead: max_ulcer_index=10 passes stocks with UI under 10. Below 5 is very smooth; above 20 means the stock has experienced deep, prolonged recent drawdowns. Unlike MDD, it penalizes slow recoveries.
ulcer_index_filter.caution: A 60-day window may miss earlier large drawdowns. In bull markets, nearly everything has low UI, reducing its discriminative power. Use 252-day lookback for a more realistic risk assessment through full market cycles.

calmar_ratio_filter.label: Calmar Ratio
calmar_ratio_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
calmar_ratio_filter.whenToUse: "Is the return worth the worst drawdown?" Calmar = Annual Return / MDD. Same return with smaller MDD = better investment. Measures risk-adjusted efficiency.
calmar_ratio_filter.howToRead: min_calmar=0.5 passes stocks where annual return is at least 0.5x their MDD. Above 1.0 is good; 2.0+ is excellent. lookback=252 (1 year) is standard.
calmar_ratio_filter.caution: Past MDD doesn't guarantee future — a stock with no prior drawdown can suddenly drop 40%. In bull markets, nearly every stock shows high Calmar. Factor in market regime.

max_drawdown_window_filter.label: Max Drawdown Window
max_drawdown_window_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
max_drawdown_window_filter.whenToUse: "Has this stock experienced a severe drop at any point recently?" Maximum drawdown over the lookback window filters out stocks with a history of large losses, regardless of current price recovery.
max_drawdown_window_filter.howToRead: max_drawdown_pct=20 passes stocks whose worst peak-to-trough loss within 120 days is under 20%. At 10%, only stocks with minimal recent pullbacks qualify. At 252 days, it covers a full year.
max_drawdown_window_filter.caution: Absence of past drawdown does not predict future safety — long-calm stocks can suddenly crash (tail risk). Use as a supplementary risk filter, never as the sole measure. A stock that hasn't dropped may simply be overdue.

return_skewness_filter.label: Return Skewness
return_skewness_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
return_skewness_filter.whenToUse: "Are returns skewed toward large losses?" Negative skewness means big drops occur more frequently than big gains. Investors naturally dislike negative skew — it is the return profile that blindsides portfolios.
return_skewness_filter.howToRead: min_skewness=-1 passes stocks with skewness above -1 (excludes severe negative skew). Near 0 is symmetric; above +0.5 means positive surprises dominate. Lottery-type stocks show high positive skew.
return_skewness_filter.caution: Skewness is highly sensitive to sample size — 60 days is statistically fragile. Use 120+ days. Paradoxically, positively skewed stocks (big upside potential) often have lower expected returns in academic research.

return_kurtosis_filter.label: Return Kurtosis
return_kurtosis_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
return_kurtosis_filter.whenToUse: "Does this stock's return distribution have fat tails — meaning extreme moves happen more often than normal?" High kurtosis indicates a leptokurtic distribution prone to sudden large gains or losses. Measures black-swan sensitivity.
return_kurtosis_filter.howToRead: max_kurtosis=10 passes stocks with kurtosis under 10 (normal distribution is 3). Below 5 is relatively well-behaved. Above 20, extreme events are common. Check whether the value uses excess kurtosis (K-3) or raw kurtosis.
return_kurtosis_filter.caution: Low past kurtosis doesn't prevent future tail events — it only describes what has already happened. With only 60 days of data, kurtosis estimates are statistically unstable. Use 120+ day windows for more reliable estimates.

intraday_return_filter.label: Intraday Return
intraday_return_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
intraday_return_filter.whenToUse: "Did the stock close higher than it opened today?" A positive intraday return (open-to-close) indicates buying pressure dominated the session — a short-term bullish signal equivalent to a bullish candle.
intraday_return_filter.howToRead: min_intraday_return_pct=0 passes stocks that closed above their open price. At 1.0, only stocks up 1%+ intraday qualify. Equivalent to filtering for bullish candlestick bodies.
intraday_return_filter.caution: Single-day signals are extremely noisy. End-of-day institutional basket trades can distort the close. Better used as a confirmation layer on already-screened stocks rather than as a primary filter.

dso_trend_filter.label: DSO Trend Filter
dso_trend_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
dso_trend_filter.whenToUse: "Is the company collecting receivables more slowly — an early warning of revenue quality decay?" Rising DSO (Days Sales Outstanding) can signal channel stuffing or deteriorating credit quality, often preceding earnings restatements.
dso_trend_filter.howToRead: min_dso_increase_pct=5 flags (and excludes) stocks where DSO rose 5%+ over the past year. Rising DSO while revenue grows is a red flag — sales may be booked but cash isn't arriving.
dso_trend_filter.caution: Normal DSO ranges vary dramatically by sector — construction can exceed 90 days while SaaS averages under 30. Focus on the rate of change, not the absolute level. Seasonal patterns within fiscal quarters can also distort readings.

ema_cross.label: EMA Cross
ema_cross.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
ema_cross.whenToUse: "Has the fast EMA crossed above the slow — signaling a momentum shift?" The EMA crossover is a classic trend-reversal signal. Unlike SMA, EMA weights recent prices more heavily, yielding faster reaction times.
ema_cross.howToRead: fast=12, slow=26 mirrors the MACD periods. direction=bullish passes stocks where the fast EMA crossed above slow within lookback_days=5. A cross above the zero line confirms established strength.
ema_cross.caution: Sideways markets generate constant crossovers that eat into trading costs (whipsaw). Use only when ADX is above 25, or add a 1-2 day confirmation hold. Frequent crosses with no follow-through are the hallmark of trendless markets.

ema_slope.label: EMA Slope
ema_slope.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
ema_slope.whenToUse: "Is the moving average itself pointing upward?" A positive EMA slope means price is trending up. Less trigger-happy than crossover signals, it directly measures the direction and velocity of the trend.
ema_slope.howToRead: min_slope_pct=0 passes stocks where the EMA is flat or rising. At 0.5 the trend is brisk; at 1.0 it is steep. period=20 for monthly trend, 50 for quarterly, 200 for secular direction.
ema_slope.caution: Slope is sensitive to a single day's spike — one gap-up can flip it positive. Use lookback_days=5+ to smooth daily noise. Combining with above_ma creates a more robust trend-confirmation setup.

sma_slope.label: SMA Slope
sma_slope.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
sma_slope.whenToUse: "Is the simple moving average pointing upward?" SMA slope measures trend direction using equally-weighted historical prices. Less reactive than EMA slope, producing fewer false signals but slower trend-change detection.
sma_slope.howToRead: min_slope_pct=0 passes stocks with a rising SMA. EMA slope reacts faster but generates more noise; SMA slope is more stable. period=50 for medium-term, 200 for long-term secular trend.
sma_slope.caution: The SMA equal-weighting means that when an extreme historical data point drops out of the window, the slope can shift abruptly (the drop-off effect). A spike from 20 days ago leaving the window can suddenly flatten the slope.

macd_signal_cross.label: MACD Signal Cross
macd_signal_cross.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
macd_signal_cross.whenToUse: "Has the MACD line crossed above its signal line?" The most famous technical trading signal. Developed by Gerald Appel in the 1970s, a bullish cross signals the start of upward momentum.
macd_signal_cross.howToRead: direction=bullish passes stocks where MACD crossed above the signal line within 5 days. A cross above the zero line confirms strength; below zero suggests an early bottoming reversal.
macd_signal_cross.caution: Sideways markets generate endless crosses near the zero line — each one costing commissions with no follow-through. The 12/26/9 parameters date from the 1970s and may not be optimal for modern markets. Pair with ADX or volume.

macd_histogram_slope.label: MACD Histogram Slope
macd_histogram_slope.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
macd_histogram_slope.whenToUse: "Is MACD momentum accelerating?" An increasing histogram means the gap between MACD and its signal line is widening — momentum is building, not just present. Catches trend acceleration before the MACD line itself crosses.
macd_histogram_slope.howToRead: min_slope=0 passes stocks where the histogram is growing. lookback=3 measures the 3-day gradient. The transition from negative to positive histogram is the earliest MACD-family buy timing.
macd_histogram_slope.caution: Histogram slope is essentially a third derivative of price, making it extremely noise-sensitive. A 3-day lookback produces many false signals — use 5+ days. Always confirm with MACD line direction.

cci_overbought_oversold.label: CCI Overbought/Oversold
cci_overbought_oversold.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
cci_overbought_oversold.whenToUse: "How far has price deviated from its statistical mean?" CCI measures deviation from average. Above +100 = overbought; below -100 = oversold. Useful for mean-reversion strategies.
cci_overbought_oversold.howToRead: mode=oversold, threshold=100 passes stocks with CCI below -100 (oversold). Switch to mode=overbought for +100+. Shorter period = more sensitive.
cci_overbought_oversold.caution: CCI can stay below -100 in strong downtrends (oversold gets more oversold). Counter-trend entries during strong trends are dangerous. Use only in low-ADX (sideways) markets or with RSI confirmation.

williams_r_reversal.label: Williams %R Reversal
williams_r_reversal.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
williams_r_reversal.whenToUse: "Is Williams %R turning up from oversold — an early reversal signal?" %R is mathematically nearly identical to Stochastic %K but on an inverted 0 to -100 scale. Larry Williams designed it for short-term mean-reversion timing.
williams_r_reversal.howToRead: direction=bullish passes stocks where %R rises from below -80 (oversold). Above -20 is overbought. Period=14 is standard. Interpretation mirrors Stochastic signals — only the scale convention differs.
williams_r_reversal.caution: Same limitations as Stochastic — %R gets stuck below -80 in strong downtrends. An oversold reading does not guarantee reversal. Always pair with a trend filter (MA direction, ADX strength) to confirm the broader context.

trix_cross.label: TRIX Cross
trix_cross.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
trix_cross.whenToUse: "A triple-smoothed momentum signal for filtering out all short-term noise." TRIX applies EMA three times and then measures the rate of change — extreme noise reduction for identifying only genuine, sustained trend changes.
trix_cross.howToRead: direction=bullish passes stocks where TRIX crossed above its signal line within 5 days. The triple EMA smoothing makes signals very rare but highly filtered. Best for weekly/monthly timeframe strategies.
trix_cross.caution: Triple smoothing means signals arrive very late — the trend may be well underway before TRIX confirms it. Unsuitable for short-term trading. Use a faster indicator (EMA cross) for timing within the TRIX-confirmed trend direction.

aroon_trend_signal.label: Aroon Trend Signal
aroon_trend_signal.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
aroon_trend_signal.whenToUse: "How recently did this stock hit a new high?" High Aroon Up means a recent peak — upward momentum is alive. Filters for stocks with fresh upside momentum.
aroon_trend_signal.howToRead: min_aroon=70 means the high occurred within the last 7-8 days of a 25-day period. 100 = today's price is the period high. direction=down for downtrend filtering.
aroon_trend_signal.caution: Aroon only tracks the timing of extremes, so a stock that spiked then flatlined stays high for a while. Pair with EMA slope for actual price trajectory.

money_flow_index_signal.label: Money Flow Index
money_flow_index_signal.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
money_flow_index_signal.whenToUse: "Is this stock oversold on a volume-weighted basis?" MFI is "RSI with volume" — it weights price movements by volume, distinguishing between genuine oversold conditions backed by actual capital flow versus price-only signals.
money_flow_index_signal.howToRead: mode=oversold at 20 passes stocks with MFI below 20 (oversold). At 80, overbought zones are flagged. Because volume is incorporated, MFI signals tend to be more reliable than RSI alone.
money_flow_index_signal.caution: Like RSI, MFI can stay below 20 in strong downtrends indefinitely. Low-liquidity stocks produce distorted volume data, undermining MFI reliability. Apply a liquidity filter before using this signal.

vwap_cross_signal.label: VWAP Cross Signal
vwap_cross_signal.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
vwap_cross_signal.whenToUse: "Has price crossed above the volume-weighted average price?" Above VWAP means the average buyer is profitable — bullish sentiment. VWAP is the benchmark institutional traders use to evaluate execution quality.
vwap_cross_signal.howToRead: lookback_days=3 passes stocks that crossed above the 20-day VWAP within 3 days. Above VWAP = majority of recent traders in profit (bullish); below = most underwater (bearish). A key institutional reference.
vwap_cross_signal.caution: Daily-bar VWAP is an approximation of the true intraday VWAP, which requires tick data. For daily screening, treat it as a 20-day volume-weighted average price reference. Precision is inherently limited.

vwap_distance_pct.label: VWAP Distance %
vwap_distance_pct.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
vwap_distance_pct.whenToUse: "How far is price from its VWAP — is it stretched or near fair value?" Distance from VWAP measures whether the stock is trading at, above, or below the average cost basis of recent volume. Institutional traders anchor decisions here.
vwap_distance_pct.howToRead: max_distance_pct=5 passes stocks within 5% of VWAP. Above VWAP by 5%+ suggests short-term overextension; below by 5%+ may attract institutional buying at perceived value.
vwap_distance_pct.caution: Same daily-bar VWAP caveat as vwap_cross. Volatile stocks naturally drift farther from VWAP, so normalize by ATR or NATR for meaningful cross-stock comparison.

relative_volume_percentile.label: Relative Volume Percentile
relative_volume_percentile.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
relative_volume_percentile.whenToUse: "Is today's volume unusually high relative to this stock's own history?" A percentile-based approach to volume analysis — more robust to outliers than simple average ratios. Tells you where today's volume ranks within its own distribution.
relative_volume_percentile.howToRead: min_percentile=70 passes stocks in the top 30% of their own 60-day volume range. At 90, only top-10% volume days qualify — clear spikes. Self-referencing, so each stock is judged against its own norm.
relative_volume_percentile.caution: Volume surges can be buying or selling panic — direction is ambiguous without price context. Options expiry, index rebalancing, and block trades create mechanical volume spikes that have no directional meaning.

turnover_ratio_min.label: Turnover Ratio Min
turnover_ratio_min.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
turnover_ratio_min.whenToUse: "Is there sufficient trading relative to shares outstanding?" Turnover ratio (daily volume / float) normalizes liquidity by float size, enabling fair comparison between a mega-cap and a micro-cap stock.
turnover_ratio_min.howToRead: min_turnover_ratio=0.01 passes stocks where 1%+ of float trades daily. Large-caps typically run 0.5-2%; speculative small-caps can hit 5-10%. This is more equitable than raw volume for cross-cap screening.
turnover_ratio_min.caution: Very high turnover can signal speculative excess rather than healthy liquidity — consider adding a max threshold. Float calculations may exclude or include treasury shares and major-holder blocks, affecting the ratio.

atr_percentile_filter.label: ATR Percentile
atr_percentile_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
atr_percentile_filter.whenToUse: "Is this stock's volatility abnormally high compared to its own history?" Uses percentile rank instead of absolute ATR — filtering out stocks in unusually volatile periods.
atr_percentile_filter.howToRead: max_percentile=80 excludes stocks in the top 20% of their 120-day ATR history. Lower to 50 for stocks in below-average volatility (calm) periods only.
atr_percentile_filter.caution: "Low volatility" isn't always safe — it could be the calm before a storm (squeeze). Too strict excludes pre-breakout opportunities. Use as position-sizing input, not primary filter.

atr_expansion_breakout.label: ATR Expansion Breakout
atr_expansion_breakout.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
atr_expansion_breakout.whenToUse: "Is volatility expanding with the breakout?" Rising ATR during a price move signals a "real" move. A volatility confirmation filter that separates genuine from fake breakouts.
atr_expansion_breakout.howToRead: atr_multiplier=1.2 passes stocks where current ATR exceeds recent average by 1.2x. Raise to 1.5 for volatility explosions only. breakout_lookback=20 sets the reference period.
atr_expansion_breakout.caution: ATR expansion can happen downward too — always pair with directional filters (above_ma, EMA slope). Earnings/news events cause one-off volatility spikes. Check the event calendar.

natr_filter.label: NATR Filter
natr_filter.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
natr_filter.whenToUse: "What is this stock's daily volatility as a percentage of its price?" NATR normalizes ATR by closing price, making volatility directly comparable across stocks of any price level — a $5 stock and a $500 stock on equal footing.
natr_filter.howToRead: max_natr_pct=5 passes stocks with average daily range under 5% of price. At 3% it's stable; 8%+ is highly volatile. Unlike raw ATR, NATR is a percentage, enabling apples-to-apples cross-stock comparison.
natr_filter.caution: Low-priced stocks tend to have structurally high NATR even if dollar moves are small. Combine with min_price to double-filter cheap, volatile names.

dmi_directional_cross.label: DMI Directional Cross
dmi_directional_cross.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
dmi_directional_cross.whenToUse: "Has bullish momentum just overtaken bearish momentum?" A DI+ crossing above DI- signals buying pressure winning over selling. Combined with ADX, this is the core entry trigger for directional trend systems.
dmi_directional_cross.howToRead: lookback_days=5 passes stocks where DI+ crossed above DI- within the last 5 days. Standard period is 14. Signal reliability jumps significantly when ADX is simultaneously above 25.
dmi_directional_cross.caution: Whipsaw crossovers are frequent when ADX is below 20 (no trend). Always use an ADX threshold alongside this filter. Waiting 2-3 days after the cross for confirmation reduces false entries.

ichimoku_cloud_breakout.label: Ichimoku Cloud Breakout
ichimoku_cloud_breakout.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
ichimoku_cloud_breakout.whenToUse: "Has price broken above the Ichimoku Cloud?" Being above the cloud signals a strong uptrend in this comprehensive Japanese technical system that simultaneously shows trend, support/resistance, and momentum.
ichimoku_cloud_breakout.howToRead: Default parameters (9/26/52) are Ichimoku Hosoda's original settings. Price above the cloud passes. A thicker cloud implies stronger support. Tenkan > Kijun adds short-term momentum confirmation.
ichimoku_cloud_breakout.caution: Three parameters invite over-optimization risk. The 26-day lagging span makes signals inherently delayed. Original parameters were calibrated to Japanese trading weeks (6-day weeks) and may need adjustment for Western markets.

ichimoku_tenkan_kijun_cross.label: Ichimoku Tenkan/Kijun Cross
ichimoku_tenkan_kijun_cross.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
ichimoku_tenkan_kijun_cross.whenToUse: "Has the Ichimoku conversion line crossed above the base line?" A bullish Tenkan/Kijun cross above the cloud is a strong signal; below the cloud, it is weak. The ideal three-line turn requires price, Tenkan, and lagging span all aligned bullishly.
ichimoku_tenkan_kijun_cross.howToRead: lookback_days=5 passes stocks with a cross in the last 5 days. The strongest setup requires price above the cloud, Tenkan above Kijun, and the lagging span above price — all three simultaneously.
ichimoku_tenkan_kijun_cross.caution: Fundamentally similar to EMA crossovers with the same whipsaw weakness in range-bound markets. Crosses inside the cloud have low reliability. Only accept crosses above the cloud, or add an ADX filter.

bollinger_squeeze_breakout.label: Bollinger Squeeze Breakout
bollinger_squeeze_breakout.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
bollinger_squeeze_breakout.whenToUse: "Catch stocks exploding from dead silence." BB squeeze (narrow band) + upper breakout = volatility contraction followed by expansion. A precursor to big moves.
bollinger_squeeze_breakout.howToRead: max_width_pct=10 passes stocks where band width is under 10% of price during breakout. Lower to 5 for extreme squeezes — rarer signals but more explosive.
bollinger_squeeze_breakout.caution: Squeeze can break downward too — direction isn't guaranteed. Confirm with volume surge. Low-liquidity stocks have wide spreads making actual entry prices unfavorable.

bollinger_percent_b.label: Bollinger Percent B
bollinger_percent_b.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
bollinger_percent_b.whenToUse: "Where is the price within the Bollinger Band?" %B normalizes position from 0 (lower) to 1 (upper). Useful for overbought/oversold judgment and band-walking detection.
bollinger_percent_b.howToRead: min=0, max=1 passes "normal" stocks within the band. min=0.8 = near upper band (strong rally); max=0.2 = near lower band (weak/bounce candidate).
bollinger_percent_b.caution: %B above 1 means upper band breakout — in strong trends, prices "walk the band" for weeks (not necessarily overbought). Interpret with ADX trend strength.

ppo_signal_cross.label: PPO Signal Cross
ppo_signal_cross.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
ppo_signal_cross.whenToUse: "MACD in percentage terms — comparing momentum across different price levels." PPO normalizes MACD to percentages, enabling direct momentum comparison between a $10 stock and a $1000 stock.
ppo_signal_cross.howToRead: lookback_days=5 passes stocks where PPO crossed above its signal line within 5 days. Interpretation is identical to MACD, but the percentage scale makes multi-stock screening and ranking fairer.
ppo_signal_cross.caution: Shares the same sideways-market whipsaw weakness as MACD. The normalization advantage is primarily useful for ranking momentum across a universe of stocks rather than generating standalone buy signals.

stochastic_cross_signal.label: Stochastic Cross Signal
stochastic_cross_signal.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
stochastic_cross_signal.whenToUse: "Has %K crossed above %D — the classic Stochastic buy signal?" A bullish cross in the oversold zone (below 20) is the textbook Stochastic entry. One of the most widely taught oscillator trading signals.
stochastic_cross_signal.howToRead: lookback_days=5 passes stocks where %K crossed above %D in the last 5 days. Crosses below 20 are most significant; above 80 they indicate potential sells. Standard settings: K=14, D=3 (Slow Stochastic).
stochastic_cross_signal.caution: Sideways markets produce constant crosses with no follow-through — pure noise. Combine with an RSI range or trend filter to only accept crosses that align with the prevailing direction. Use Slow (D=3 smoothed), not Fast Stochastic.

stochrsi_signal.label: StochRSI Signal
stochrsi_signal.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
stochrsi_signal.whenToUse: "Need a faster oscillator than RSI?" StochRSI applies Stochastic math to RSI itself, creating a double-oscillator that reaches extreme zones faster. Purpose-built for short-term timing in swing-trading setups.
stochrsi_signal.howToRead: mode=oversold passes stocks where StochRSI is in its oversold zone. Signals appear faster and more frequently than RSI alone. Standard: rsi_period=14, stoch_period=14. Best suited for active swing trading.
stochrsi_signal.caution: The increased sensitivity means dramatically more false signals — StochRSI can flip from oversold to overbought in a single day. Never use as a standalone signal. Mandatory to combine with trend direction and volume confirmation.

aroon_oscillator_signal.label: Aroon Oscillator Signal
aroon_oscillator_signal.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
aroon_oscillator_signal.whenToUse: "Is the uptrend or downtrend winning?" Aroon Oscillator = Aroon Up - Aroon Down. Positive = bullish dominance. Captures both direction and strength of trend.
aroon_oscillator_signal.howToRead: min_oscillator=30 passes stocks where uptrend clearly dominates. +100 = perfect uptrend; -100 = perfect downtrend. Shorter period = faster response.
aroon_oscillator_signal.caution: Whipsaws near zero in sideways markets. Only considers the location of highs/lows within the period, ignoring price action between them. Combine with ADX.

ultimate_oscillator_signal.label: Ultimate Oscillator Signal
ultimate_oscillator_signal.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
ultimate_oscillator_signal.whenToUse: "What does buying pressure look like across three timeframes simultaneously?" Larry Williams's Ultimate Oscillator combines 7-, 14-, and 28-day buying pressure into a single multi-timeframe momentum reading.
ultimate_oscillator_signal.howToRead: min_value=50 passes stocks with UO above 50 (buying pressure dominates). Below 30 is oversold; above 70 is overbought. Williams's original strategy requires a three-step bullish divergence confirmation before entry.
ultimate_oscillator_signal.caution: The original UO trading rules are complex (divergence + level confirmation). A simple level filter misses the indicator's true design intent. For full benefit, implement the divergence logic, or use as a supplementary filter only.

chaikin_money_flow_signal.label: Chaikin Money Flow
chaikin_money_flow_signal.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
chaikin_money_flow_signal.whenToUse: "Are institutions putting money in or pulling it out?" CMF is volume-weighted closing position. Positive = buying pressure dominates. Directly measures money flow direction.
chaikin_money_flow_signal.howToRead: min_cmf=0 passes stocks with positive CMF (buying pressure). Above 0.1 = clear inflow. period=20 is monthly; shorten to 10 for near-term flow shifts.
chaikin_money_flow_signal.caution: Late-session closing price manipulation (window dressing) can distort CMF. A few large trades can flip CMF in small-caps. Cross-check with AD Line and OBV.

chaikin_oscillator_signal.label: Chaikin Oscillator
chaikin_oscillator_signal.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
chaikin_oscillator_signal.whenToUse: "Is money inflow accelerating?" Chaikin Oscillator = fast EMA - slow EMA of AD Line. Positive = inflow accelerating. Captures the rate of change in money flow.
chaikin_oscillator_signal.howToRead: min_value=0 passes stocks where inflow is accelerating. fast=3/slow=10 is standard. The moment value crosses from negative to positive is the buy timing signal.
chaikin_oscillator_signal.caution: Similar structure to MACD, sharing its sideways-market whipsaw weakness. AD Line can't capture gaps, so gap-up/gap-down periods may distort readings.

ad_line_trend.label: A/D Line Trend
ad_line_trend.help: Practical summary for based on the issue-487 research guide. Sources:
ad_line_trend.whenToUse: "Is money actually flowing in while the price rises?" An upward AD Line confirms sustained buying pressure. Validates whether price and money flow align.
ad_line_trend.howToRead: lookback_days=20 passes stocks where the AD Line trends up over 20 days. Shorten to 10 for short-term flow changes; extend to 40 for medium-term confirmation.
ad_line_trend.caution: AD Line only reflects closing price position, missing gaps. Unreliable for low-volume stocks. Cross-check with OBV or CMF for confirmation.

volume_ma_ratio.label: Volume MA Ratio
volume_ma_ratio.desc: Volume short MA / long MA ratio range filter
volume_ma_ratio.help: Measures whether short-term volume is overheating or drying up versus baseline.
volume_ma_ratio.whenToUse: Is current trading activity meaningfully different from baseline? Useful for momentum confirmation or risk throttling.
volume_ma_ratio.howToRead: Example: if short_period=5, long_period=20, ratio=1.5 means short-term volume is 50% above baseline. Raising min_ratio requires stronger participation.
volume_ma_ratio.caution: Different sectors have different natural turnover profiles. Use with price filters to avoid low-quality churn signals.

return_pct_range.label: Return % Range
return_pct_range.help: Filters names by bounded return range over a configurable lookback period.
return_pct_range.whenToUse: Is recent performance within a tradable range? Useful for mean-reversion selection and risk-bucket construction.
return_pct_range.howToRead: Example: lookback_days=5, min_return_pct=-3, max_return_pct=5 keeps names with 5-day return between -3% and +5%. Widening bounds increases candidates.
return_pct_range.caution: Return alone is regime-sensitive and may overfit. Combine with trend/volume or quality filters and account for earnings/event gaps.

supertrend_signal.label: Supertrend Signal
supertrend_signal.desc: Detect a bullish or bearish price crossover against the Supertrend line within recent days.
supertrend_signal.help: Uses ATR-based dynamic bands. Match when close crosses the Supertrend line in the selected direction during the lookback window.
supertrend_signal.whenToUse: Is the trend truly turning up or down now? Use this for trend-following entries, pullback re-entry filters, and risk-control exits. Supertrend is a practical ATR trend tool widely used by discretionary and systematic traders in momentum and risk-management strategies.
supertrend_signal.howToRead: Example: period=10, multiplier=3.0, lookback_days=3, direction=bullish means "pass if price crossed above Supertrend within the last 3 bars." Increasing period or multiplier smooths signals and reduces noise but gives later entries; decreasing them reacts faster but increases whipsaws. Fast-moving growth/IT names often need a wider multiplier (for example 3.0-4.0), while lower-volatility defensive sectors may work with tighter settings (for example 2.0-3.0). As a reference, many charting defaults use period 10 and multiplier 3.0.
supertrend_signal.caution: A crossover is not a guaranteed reversal; sideways markets can cause repeated false flips. Combine with volume/trend confirmation (for example relative volume or MA alignment) to reduce whipsaw risk. Sector volatility regimes differ, so one parameter set should not be reused blindly across all industries. Data quality matters: bad OHLC candles, split adjustment errors, or missing bars can distort ATR and produce incorrect signals.

price_lag_compare.label: Price Lag Compare
price_lag_compare.desc: Compare OHLC price at two different lag points
price_lag_compare.help: Compare two past price points without moving averages.
price_lag_compare.whenToUse: Detect momentum shifts (e.g., yesterday's close below 3-day-ago close).
price_lag_compare.howToRead: field=close, lag_a=1, lag_b=3, operator=lt → yesterday's close < close 3 days ago.
price_lag_compare.caution: Single lag comparisons generate false signals in choppy markets.

volume_lag_compare.label: Volume Lag Compare
volume_lag_compare.desc: Compare volume at two different lag points
volume_lag_compare.help: Compares historical volume points to detect participation changes.
volume_lag_compare.whenToUse: Detect volume surges or declines relative to a prior session.
volume_lag_compare.howToRead: lag_a=1, lag_b=5, operator=gt → yesterday's volume > volume 5 days ago.
volume_lag_compare.caution: Volume comparisons are noisy around holidays and earnings.

indicators.rsiExplain: RSI measures momentum on a 0–100 scale. Below 30 signals oversold (buy opportunity), above 70 signals overbought (sell opportunity).
indicators.macdExplain: MACD tracks trend direction. When MACD crosses above the Signal line, it suggests upward momentum (bullish). Below means bearish.
indicators.bollingerExplain: Think of Bollinger Bands as a price highway. If the price goes above the upper line, it may be too expensive. If below the lower line, it may be a bargain. Currently the price is in the normal zone.
indicators.maExplain: SMAs smooth out price data to identify trends. Price above the average usually indicates an uptrend. 5-day is short term, 200-day is long term.
indicators.volumeExplain: Volume measures how many shares are traded. High volume confirms trend strength.
